proposal.utterance: There is no real influence of one created substance upon another in metaphysical strictness.

entities.label: RealInfluence
entities.rationale: Real causal influence between substances is a process (an occurrent happening in which one substance acts upon another). The utterance denies that instances of this class exist between created substances in metaphysical strictness.

entities.label: CreatedSubstance
entities.rationale: Leibniz distinguishes created substances from God (the uncreated substance). Created substances are the finite, individual material/immaterial entities in nature. NaturalMaterialEntity is the closest existing parent.

entities.label: IntersubstantialInfluenceAbsence
entities.rationale: The metaphysical thesis that no real influence passes between created substances is best represented as a quality (a constraint on the ontological status of RealInfluence relations among created substances): specifically the absence of causal dependence between them. Modeled as an individual quality inhering in the class of created substances collectively.

relations.rationale: Created substances are a subtype of natural material entities in this ontology; they exclude God (NecessaryBeing).
The absence of real influence is typed as a Quality inhering in the domain of created substances.

This quality of having no real mutual influence inheres in created substances as a class-level constraint (no instance of RealInfluence has a created substance as both its agent and patient in metaphysical strictness).

open_questions: Should CreatedSubstance be a subclass of IndivisibleSubstance or SimpleSubstance rather than NaturalMaterialEntity, given that Leibniz's created substances (monads) may not be straightforwardly material in the BFO sense?

Should RealInfluence be modeled as a class with an explicit disjointness or cardinality constraint asserting no instances hold between distinct CreatedSubstance individuals, rather than via a quality of absence?

Is 'metaphysical strictness' a modal qualifier that should be encoded separately (e.g., as a OriginConstraint or a new ModalConstraint disposition class), distinguishing phenomenal/apparent influence from real influence?

Should the existing individual 'PreEstablishedHarmony' or a related concept be introduced here as the explanatory mechanism Leibniz offers in place of real influence (i.e., PerfectMutualAccord already in the graph)?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance expresses Leibniz's doctrine that no genuine causal influence passes between one created substance and another — each substance unfolds from its own internal principle. Three new entities are proposed: (1) the class CreatedSubstance (BFO material entity, subclass of NaturalMaterialEntity, distinguishing finite substances from God/NecessaryBeing), (2) the class RealInfluence (a BFO process representing genuine inter-substantial causal action, whose instances Leibniz denies exist between created substances), and (3) the individual IntersubstantialInfluenceAbsence (a quality inhering in CreatedSubstance encoding the metaphysical constraint). The existing individual PerfectMutualAccord is already in the graph and represents Leibniz's positive account of why substances appear to interact; this proposal focuses on the negative ontological claim. Several open questions are raised about modal encoding and the exact BFO parent for monad-like created substances.

proposal.utterance: All things are continually produced by the power of God.

entities.label: ContinualProduction
entities.rationale: The continual production of all things by God is an ongoing process — a happening that unfolds in time. It is best modeled as a Process class (BFO_0000015), as it describes a general kind of event (God's sustaining creative act) rather than a single dated occurrence.

relations.rationale: ContinualProduction is a subclass of Process (BFO_0000015).

God (an existing individual of type BFO_0000040) participates in ContinualProduction as the agent/cause. RO_0000056 (participates in) links a continuant to a process. Note: this asserts God participates in every instance of ContinualProduction; the claim is universal.

UniversalCausation (an existing disposition/role individual of type BFO_0000016) is realized in the ContinualProduction process, since the utterance asserts God's power (captured as UniversalCausation) is what drives this production.

open_questions: Should ContinualProduction be treated as a single universal individual process (the ongoing sustaining act of God across all time) rather than a class of process instances? The utterance's 'continually' suggests an ongoing process, but it could also be modeled as a universal process individual.

Is 'power of God' best captured by the existing individual working:UniversalCausation (typed as BFO_0000016 Disposition), or should a new individual such as 'DivinePower' or 'DivinePotentia' be minted? The existing 'DivineEssence' and 'DivineWill' are also relevant candidates.

Does 'all things' include both material entities and souls/minds, or only corporeal substances? This affects whether participants in ContinualProduction should be universally quantified over all BFO_0000002 continuants.
Is ContinualProduction the same as or a subtype of the existing working:Creation class, or should it be modeled as a distinct process of conservation/sustenance distinct from initial creation?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that God continually produces (sustains in existence) all things through divine power. Ontologically, this commits us to: (1) a Process class ContinualProduction (BFO_0000015) representing God's ongoing sustaining causal activity; (2) the existing individual God (BFO_0000040) as participant in this process via RO_0000056; and (3) the existing individual UniversalCausation (BFO_0000016) as the disposition realized in ContinualProduction. I avoid creating a new 'DivinePower' individual because UniversalCausation already captures God's causal capacity. I flag open questions about whether ContinualProduction is a subtype of the existing Creation class, whether it should be an individual rather than a class, and which existing individual best represents 'the power of God' in this context.

proposal.utterance: God created each soul such that everything within it comes from its own substance through perfect spontaneity.

entities.label: PerfectSpontaneity
entities.rationale: Perfect spontaneity is the internally-grounded capacity of a soul to produce all its states from within its own substance without external efficient causation. This is a disposition (internally grounded realizable entity) inhering in Soul.

entities.label: SoulCreation
entities.rationale: The act by which God creates each soul is a process, specifically an instance of the existing Creation class. It is the event in which God is the agent and Soul is the product.

entities.label: SoulSubstanceContent
entities.rationale: The claim that 'everything within the soul comes from its own substance' asserts a disposition or immanent generative capacity of the soul's own substance—the soul's intrinsic power to produce all its states internally. This is distinct from PerfectSpontaneity (the modal character of the generation) and captures the substance-grounded source principle.

relations.rationale: God participates in the SoulCreation process as the creating agent.
Soul participates in SoulCreation as the entity brought into being.
PerfectSpontaneity inheres in Soul as a disposition of its substance.
The soul's capacity to generate all its states from its own substance inheres in Soul.
The creation of each soul is part of the broader DivineOrdering process already in the ontology.

open_questions: Should 'PerfectSpontaneity' and 'SoulSubstanceContent' be merged into a single disposition, since both capture aspects of the soul's immanent generative power? Or is the distinction between the modal character (spontaneity) and the substantive source (own substance) worth preserving as two separate dispositions?

Is 'Soul' intended here as a universal class (every soul has this property) or as the single individual 'Soul' already in the ontology? If universal, we should mint a Soul class with these dispositions as universally inhering.
Does the spontaneity disposition get realized in ThoughtSuccession or some other MentalChange process already in the ontology?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts three ontological commitments: (1) God performs an act of creating souls (mapped to a SoulCreation individual of type Creation/Process, with God and Soul as participants); (2) each soul has an internally-grounded capacity such that all its states derive from its own substance (SoulSubstanceContent, a Disposition inhering in Soul); and (3) this self-generation occurs through perfect spontaneity (PerfectSpontaneity, a distinct Disposition inhering in Soul capturing the modal character of autonomous causation). Both dispositions are BFO_0000016 because they are internally grounded in the soul's own nature rather than externally assigned roles. The SoulCreation process is linked to the existing DivineOrdering individual as a part. Existing individuals God and Soul are reused; no new classes are minted because the utterance describes specific individuals in Leibniz's system.

proposal.utterance: Internal feelings in the soul arise from its own proper original constitution given at creation.

entities.label: InternalFeeling
entities.rationale: Internal feelings are affective states inhering in the soul/mind, best typed as a subclass of MentalAffection (itself a Quality). Distinct from Thought or Idea because they are affective/phenomenal rather than representational.

entities.label: OriginalConstitution
entities.rationale: The 'proper original constitution given at creation' is the intrinsic, internally-grounded structural basis of the soul that disposes it toward certain internal feelings. This is a disposition (internally grounded realizable entity) inhering in Soul. Modeled as an individual because the text refers to a singular constitutive fact of the soul.

relations.rationale: The original constitution inheres in the Soul as its bearer, per BFO disposition semantics.
Internal feelings are a subkind of MentalAffection (Quality inhering in soul/mind).

The original constitution is realized in (or more precisely, originates in) the Creation process. BFO_0000054 (realized in) links the disposition to the process in which it comes about; here Creation is the relevant process individual already in the ontology.

open_questions: Should OriginalConstitution be a class (a type of disposition souls can have) rather than an individual? If every soul has its own original constitution, a class would be more appropriate.

Is InternalFeeling meant to be strictly phenomenal/affective (a Quality), or does it also involve a process of feeling (which would make it a MentalChange/Process)? The utterance suggests it is a standing state arising from constitution, which favors Quality.

Should OriginalConstitution be related to the existing individual 'Creation' (the process), or does Leibniz intend a separate divine-bestowal event distinct from what 'Creation' already captures in the ontology?

Should there be a disposition-to-quality causal link between OriginalConstitution and InternalFeeling? BFO does not have a direct 'causes' predicate; we could use a custom relation or RO_0002410 (causally related to) if RO is in scope.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance makes two ontological commitments: (1) there is a kind of mental state — internal feelings — that arises in the soul, and (2) these arise from a prior intrinsic structural property of the soul that was given at creation. OriginalConstitution inheres in Soul and is linked to the existing Creation process as the event in which it is bestowed. The existing individuals Soul and Creation are reused without modification.

proposal.utterance: Each substance represents the entire universe according to its own point of view.

entities.label: PerspectivalRepresentation
entities.rationale: The capacity of each substance to represent (mirror) the entire universe from its own point of view is an internally grounded disposition — a structural feature of the substance itself. It is realized in the substance's perceptual/representational activity.

entities.label: PointOfView
entities.rationale: A point of view is a perspective that inheres in a particular substance — it is a quality (a specific relational/positional property) that individuates how that substance represents the universe. It is not a process or a role but a qualitative feature belonging to exactly one substance.

entities.label: UniverseRepresentation
entities.rationale: The representational content — the 'picture' of the entire universe that each substance carries — is an information-like pattern (a generically dependent continuant) that can in principle be instantiated or expressed by any substance, but is concretely tokened in each substance. This is the content of the representation, distinct from the disposition to represent.

relations.rationale: PerspectivalRepresentation is a subclass of Disposition, inheriting BFO_0000016.
PointOfView is a subclass of Quality, inheriting BFO_0000019.
UniverseRepresentation is a subclass of Generically dependent continuant, inheriting BFO_0000031.

entities.label: SeparateWorld
entities.rationale: Each spirit being 'a separate world' is a relational quality of independence or self-sufficiency that inheres in the spirit. It is not a site but a property of complete self-containment.

entities.label: Independence
entities.rationale: The claim that each spirit is 'independent of others' is modeled as a quality of independence inhering in spirits. This is a distinct ontological commitment from SeparateWorld but closely related.

entities.label: EnclosureOfInfinite
entities.rationale: The capacity to 'enclose the infinite' is an internally grounded capacity or disposition of a spirit — it can express or represent the infinite universe, which is a dispositional property grounded in the spirit's nature. Relates to Potentiality and SubstanceProgress already in the ontology.

relations.rationale: Spirit is typed as a subclass of material entity (independent continuant), consistent with how Soul and Mind are modeled.
SeparateWorld is a quality inhering in spirits.
Being a separate world entails independence; SeparateWorld is a subclass of Independence.
Independence is a quality inhering in substances.
Enclosing the infinite is a specific form of potentiality already recognised in the ontology.
Leibnizian spirits are simple substances (indivisible, non-extended); Spirit is a subclass of SimpleSubstance already in the ontology.

open_questions: Should 'Spirit' be modeled as a subclass of 'SimpleSubstance' (already in ontology, indivisible) or directly of 'Mind'? In Leibniz spirits are rational monads, suggesting alignment with both Mind and SimpleSubstance.

Is 'SeparateWorld' best captured as a Quality (a property of self-containment) or as a Role (an externally-grounded functional identity)? The Leibnizian text suggests it is intrinsic, favoring Quality/Disposition.
Should 'EnclosureOfInfinite' be linked to the existing individual 'Universe' to express that each spirit represents or mirrors the universe?

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts three properties of every spirit: (1) it constitutes a separate world unto itself, (2) it is independent of all other spirits, and (3) it encloses or expresses the infinite. These are universal claims about the class Spirit. Spirit is modeled as a new class, a subclass of SimpleSubstance (already present) since Leibnizian spirits are rational simple substances akin to monads. The 'separate world' property and 'independence' are modeled as quality classes inhering in spirits; SeparateWorld is made a subclass of Independence since being a self-contained world entails independence. The capacity to enclose the infinite is modeled as a disposition (EnclosureOfInfinite), made a subclass of the existing Potentiality class, since it is an internally-grounded capacity of each spirit's nature. No new individuals are warranted as the statement is a universal generalization. Several open questions are flagged regarding the precise BFO placement of these entities.

proposal.utterance: Perfect harmony of substances without mutual communication requires a common cause.

entities.label: PerfectHarmonyOfSubstances
entities.rationale: Perfect harmony of substances is a relational quality inhering in the collection of substances (the Universe). It is a specifically dependent continuant quality of that material entity. Distinct from PerfectMutualAccord which already exists, but this is the harmony predicated of all substances collectively as a system property.

entities.label: MutualCommunication
entities.rationale: Mutual communication (intersubstantial causal interaction) is a process type. The utterance posits its absence; we need the class to express the negation and link to harmony.

entities.label: AbsenceOfMutualCommunication
entities.rationale: The condition of substances lacking mutual causal communication is a disposition-like constraint on the system. Modeled as a disposition (realizable entity) that is not realized, grounding the harmony.

entities.label: CommonCause
entities.rationale: Common cause is a role played by some entity (God/NecessaryBeing) that grounds the harmony of substances. It is an externally grounded role.

entities.label: CommonCauseRole
entities.rationale: The specific instance of the CommonCause role as required by the harmony of substances, borne by God/NecessaryBeing.

relations.rationale: The perfect harmony of substances inheres in the Universe (the totality of substances) as a quality of that whole.
PerfectHarmonyOfSubstances is a more specific articulation of PerfectMutualAccord in the context of the no-communication thesis; relating it as a subtype/instance of that quality.
The condition of no mutual communication inheres in the Universe as a system-level disposition (constraint on the substances).

God (or NecessaryBeing) bears the CommonCause role — the utterance asserts that harmony without mutual communication requires a common cause, and God is the existing individual in the ontology best suited to bear this role.
The individual CommonCauseRole is an instance of the CommonCause role class.

open_questions: Should 'perfect harmony of substances' be identified with the existing individual PerfectMutualAccord, or is it a distinct individual? The utterance seems to be elaborating on the ground of PerfectMutualAccord rather than introducing a wholly new quality.
Is 'common cause' always God/NecessaryBeing in this context (Leibnizian pre-established harmony), or should CommonCause be left as a class whose bearer is to be determined?

Should AbsenceOfMutualCommunication be modeled as a Disposition (unrealized) or rather as a Quality (a static property of the substance system)? BFO Disposition implies a potential for a process; a permanent structural absence might be better as a Quality.
Should MutualCommunication be a subclass of LegalProcess, or kept directly under BFO Process? In this context it is a metaphysical/natural process, not a legal one.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance expresses a Leibnizian metaphysical principle: that the perfect harmony observed among substances, given that they do not causally interact (no mutual communication), must be grounded in a common cause. Ontologically this introduces: (1) PerfectHarmonyOfSubstances as a quality inhering in the Universe (related to the existing PerfectMutualAccord); (2) AbsenceOfMutualCommunication as a disposition/constraint on the Universe expressing the lack of inter-substance causation; (3) CommonCause as a role class, with an individual CommonCauseRole borne by God/NecessaryBeing. The existing individuals God, NecessaryBeing, Universe, and PerfectMutualAccord are reused. The key philosophical claim — that harmony without communication requires a common cause — is represented as the CommonCauseRole inhering in God being the explanatory ground for PerfectHarmonyOfSubstances given AbsenceOfMutualCommunication. Open questions are raised about whether PerfectHarmonyOfSubstances collapses into PerfectMutualAccord and how best to type the absence condition.

proposal.utterance: In body collisions, each body suffers only from its own elasticity and internal motion.

entities.label: Elasticity
entities.rationale: Elasticity is an internally grounded capacity of a body to resist deformation and return to shape — paradigmatically a disposition in BFO terms.

entities.label: InternalMotion
entities.rationale: Internal motion is a process unfolding within the body — a temporal occurrence that is part of the body's own activity, distinct from externally imposed motion.

entities.label: BodyCollision
entities.rationale: A collision between bodies is a process (a temporal happening involving two or more material entities as participants).

entities.label: CollisionEffect
entities.rationale: The suffering or undergoing of change by a body in a collision is itself a process — specifically the sub-process each body undergoes, caused by its own elasticity and internal motion rather than by direct external imposition. Modeled as a process part of BodyCollision.

relations.rationale: InternalMotion is a kind of Process.
BodyCollision is a kind of Process.
CollisionEffect is a kind of Process.
Each CollisionEffect is part of a BodyCollision — it is a sub-process occurring within the overarching collision process.
Elasticity is a Disposition.
The collision effect (what the body suffers) realizes the body's own elasticity disposition — the disposition is the internal ground of the effect, per Leibniz's principle.

proposal.rationale_summary: Leibniz's claim that in collisions each body suffers only from its own elasticity and internal motion asserts that: (1) a BodyCollision is a process involving multiple material bodies; (2) within that process, each body undergoes a CollisionEffect that is a sub-process (part of the collision); (3) the cause of that CollisionEffect is internal — specifically the body's Elasticity (a disposition, internally grounded per BFO_0000016) and its InternalMotion (a process already ongoing within the body). No new external causal quality is posited; the effect is the realization of an already-possessed disposition. I therefore mint four new classes: BodyCollision, CollisionEffect, Elasticity, and InternalMotion, and assert that CollisionEffect is part of BodyCollision and realizes Elasticity. The existing individuals Body, ActiveForce, and SubstanceProgress are conceptually adjacent but are distinct enough that new classes are warranted rather than reuse.

proposal.utterance: Spiritual beings may make efforts.

entities.label: SpiritualBeing
entities.rationale: A spiritual being is a kind of entity that persists through time and has independent existence. Given the ontological context (Soul, God, NecessaryBeing are already typed as BFO_0000040), spiritual beings are modeled as independent continuants. Debate exists about whether they are material; BFO_0000040 is the closest fit for an independent, self-subsistent substance. Flagged in open_questions.

entities.label: Effort
entities.rationale: An effort is an internally grounded capacity or tendency of an entity to act—it is the directed, striving disposition toward action. It inheres in its bearer (the spiritual being) and is realized in some process. This fits BFO Disposition better than Role (externally grounded) or Process (effort is the capacity, not the exercise itself). Flagged in open_questions whether effort should instead be a Process (the exercising of that capacity).

relations.rationale: Effort is a subclass of Disposition: an internally grounded tendency inhering in a bearer.
Spiritual beings are independent continuants (substances that persist through time).

The statement 'spiritual beings may make efforts' entails that members of SpiritualBeing can bear an Effort disposition. Expressed as an OWL subClassOf restriction: SpiritualBeing subClassOf (bearer_of some Effort), i.e., RO_0000053 some working:Effort. This is a 'may' (existential), not a universal obligation.

open_questions: Should 'SpiritualBeing' be typed as BFO_0000040 (Material entity) or BFO_0000141 (Immaterial entity) / BFO_0000004 (Independent continuant directly)? Given that souls, God, and NecessaryBeing are already BFO_0000040 in this ontology, the convention seems to use BFO_0000040, but philosophically immaterial substances might warrant BFO_0000141 or a direct subclass of BFO_0000004.

Should 'Effort' be typed as a Disposition (BFO_0000016, the capacity/tendency to strive) or as a Process (BFO_0000015, the actual striving event)? The utterance 'may make efforts' is ambiguous: it could mean they possess the disposition to make efforts, or that efforts as occurrents are things they participate in.
Is 'SpiritualBeing' a new class, or should it be identified with existing individuals such as Soul, God, or NecessaryBeing—or should those become instances of this new class?

Does 'may make efforts' assert a universal disposition (all spiritual beings have this capacity) or merely a possibility (some spiritual beings can have it)? This affects whether we use a universal restriction or an existential one.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance 'Spiritual beings may make efforts' introduces two new ontological commitments: (1) a class SpiritualBeing typed as BFO_0000040 (following the existing convention in this ontology of placing soul-like substances under material entity), and (2) a class Effort typed as BFO_0000016 Disposition (an internally grounded tendency to act, inhering in a bearer and realizable in a process). The modal 'may' indicates an existential rather than universal claim, so SpiritualBeing is linked to Effort via an existential restriction on RO_0000053 (bearer of). Key open questions concern the proper BFO supertype for SpiritualBeing (material vs. immaterial), whether Effort is better a Disposition or a Process subtype, and how SpiritualBeing relates to already-committed individuals like Soul, God, and NecessaryBeing.

proposal.utterance: Mind can make efforts to move the body, and the body can have contrary efforts that resist.

entities.label: MindBodyEffort
entities.rationale: An effort of the mind to move the body is a process — a happening in time where the mind exerts causal influence on the body.

entities.label: BodyResistanceEffort
entities.rationale: The body's contrary effort resisting the mind is also a process — a countervailing happening that opposes the mind's effort.

entities.label: MotiveCapacity
entities.rationale: The capacity of the mind to exert effort toward moving the body is an internally-grounded disposition inhering in the mind.

entities.label: BodyResistanceDisposition
entities.rationale: The body's capacity to resist the mind's efforts is an internally-grounded disposition inhering in the body.

relations.rationale: The motive capacity (disposition of mind) is realized in the process of mind-body effort.
The body's resistance disposition is realized in the body resistance effort process.
The existing individual Soul is typed as a Mind (already extant class), consistent with the context where Soul is the thinking/willing entity that exerts mental effort.
Mind-body effort is a subtype of MentalChange, as it originates from the mind's volitional act.
The Soul (as mind) participates in the mind-body effort process as its agent/bearer.
The Body participates in the body resistance effort process as its bearer.

open_questions: Is 'effort' here best modeled as a process (happening in time) or as a disposition (capacity to resist/move)? The utterance suggests both: the effort is the actualization of a capacity, so both levels are modeled here — is this intended?
Should MindBodyEffort be a subclass of MentalChange, LegalProcess, or a new top-level subclass of BFO Process? Currently placed under MentalChange since it originates from mind.
Is the body's resistance purely mechanical (physical process) or also intentional? This affects whether BodyResistanceEffort should have a disposition subtype or be purely a physical process.
Should Soul be typed as an instance of Mind (as proposed), or is Soul distinct from Mind in this ontology?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts two kinds of causal agency: (1) the mind can exert effort to move the body, and (2) the body can have contrary efforts that resist. In BFO, effort-as-capacity is a Disposition (BFO_0000016), while effort-as-happening is a Process (BFO_0000015). Both levels are needed: MotiveCapacity inheres in the mind and is realized in MindBodyEffort; BodyResistanceDisposition inheres in the body and is realized in BodyResistanceEffort. Existing individuals Soul and Body are linked as participants. Soul is also proposed to be typed as a Mind (existing class), consistent with prior ontology context. MindBodyEffort is placed as a subclass of MentalChange since it originates from mental volition. The body resistance is a separate process class, with its own disposition. These are class-level proposals since the utterance speaks generically about mind and body interaction, not specific episodes.

entities.label: Clock
entities.rationale: A clock is a kind of material entity — it has mass and spatial extent. It is a physical assemblage of parts.

entities.label: Assemblage
entities.rationale: An assemblage is a material entity composed of multiple parts lacking intrinsic unifying principle — contrasted with a substance having TrueUnity. Modeling it as a subclass of BFO material entity with the distinguishing feature of lacking TrueUnity.

relations.rationale: The utterance asserts a clock is (nothing but) an assemblage, making Clock a subclass of Assemblage.
An assemblage is a material entity — composed of physical parts with mass and spatial extent.
Clock inherits material entity typing via Assemblage; stated explicitly for clarity.

open_questions: Should Assemblage be modeled as a disjoint class from working:TrueUnity-bearing substances (i.e., assert that Assemblage and TrueUnity are disjoint, or that no Assemblage bears a TrueUnity quality)? This would formally encode the 'not a substance with true unity' claim.

Is 'Assemblage' here a Leibnizian technical term (a mere aggregate lacking intrinsic unity), or a general compositional term? If Leibnizian, should it be explicitly contrasted with working:IndivisibleSubstance via a disjointness axiom?
Should working:NaturalMaterialEntity and working:Assemblage be declared disjoint, since natural substances (e.g., animals, monads) possess TrueUnity while artifacts/aggregates do not?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance makes two ontological claims: (1) a clock is an assemblage — a mere aggregate of parts — and (2) it is not a substance with true unity. In BFO terms, both assemblages and substances with true unity are material entities (BFO_0000040), but the distinction lies in whether they bear the TrueUnity quality (already in the ontology as working:TrueUnity, a BFO_0000019 Quality). I introduce Clock as a subclass of a new class Assemblage (itself a subclass of BFO_0000040), capturing the first claim. The second claim — that clocks lack TrueUnity — is the negation of a quality-bearing relation; this requires a disjointness or negative property restriction (e.g., no Clock bears a TrueUnity) which should be confirmed before asserting, hence placed in open_questions. No existing individuals are reused since Clock and Assemblage are kinds, not individuals.

proposal.utterance: Substances have an exact correspondence among themselves by laws of their own received at the beginning.

entities.label: ExactCorrespondence
entities.rationale: The 'exact correspondence among themselves' is a relational quality inhering in the collection of substances — a Quality (BFO_0000019). It captures the mutual mirroring/harmony Leibniz describes.

entities.label: LawsOfSubstances
entities.rationale: The 'laws of their own received at the beginning' are information-like content (rules/patterns) that can in principle be instantiated in multiple bearers; a Generically Dependent Continuant (BFO_0000031) is the best fit. This is distinct from the individual RuleOfMotion/RuleOfRest already in the ontology in that it specifically concerns the internal laws governing individual substances.

entities.label: InitialDetermination
entities.rationale: The receiving of laws 'at the beginning' refers to a founding temporal process — the initial setting/bestowal of those laws upon substances at creation. Modeled as a Process (BFO_0000015).

relations.rationale: The exact correspondence inheres in the totality of substances, approximated here by the existing individual Universe.
The substance-internal laws are part of the broader principal teleological ordering established by God — they are a component of that ordering.
The InitialDetermination process has LawsOfSubstances as its output/participant — it is the process by which those laws were conferred.
God participates in the InitialDetermination process as the agent who bestows the laws at the beginning (cf. existing individual God).
ExactCorrespondence is a part of (or grounding for) PerfectMutualAccord already in the ontology — the exact correspondence among substances constitutes or contributes to the perfect mutual accord.

The LawsOfSubstances (a realizable-like GDC) are realized in / manifest as the ExactCorrespondence quality; using realized-in loosely to capture that the laws produce the correspondence. NOTE: BFO_0000054 strictly applies to Realizable Entities; flag for review.

open_questions: Should 'ExactCorrespondence' be modeled as a class (a kind of quality that each substance pair instantiates) rather than a single individual? The statement seems to describe a general fact about all substances.

Should 'LawsOfSubstances' be typed as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) inhering in each substance rather than a GDC, since each substance has its own internal law? The text says 'laws of their own', suggesting each substance bears its own law.
Is 'InitialDetermination' the same event as the existing 'Creation' individual, or is it a separate bestowal-of-laws event that occurs at or after creation?

The final relation uses BFO_0000054 (realized in) between a GDC and a Quality, which is a BFO type mismatch. Should LawsOfSubstances instead be reclassified as a Disposition so that realized-in is applicable?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance (from Leibniz's Monadology/Discourse tradition) asserts three interconnected facts: (1) substances share an exact correspondence with one another, (2) this correspondence follows from internal laws proper to each substance, and (3) those laws were received/established at the beginning (by God). I model the correspondence as a Quality (individual ExactCorrespondence) inhering in the Universe, the laws as a Generically Dependent Continuant (individual LawsOfSubstances) that is part of the existing PrincipalTeleologicalOrdering, and the bestowal event as a Process (InitialDetermination) in which God participates. Key open questions concern whether LawsOfSubstances should instead be a Disposition inhering in each substance (since the text says 'their own'), and whether ExactCorrespondence should be a class rather than a single individual.

Laws operative in souls/forms are concretely instantiated in simple substances (souls). Flagged for review.

open_questions: Should LawOfNature be typed as BFO_0000031 (generically dependent continuant, i.e. an abstract information-like pattern) or as BFO_0000016 (disposition, i.e. an internally-grounded tendency of matter/soul to behave in certain ways)? Leibniz's laws of nature might be better understood as dispositions or as abstract patterns.

The 'like laws in souls or forms' — does this mean the same law types apply analogically to both domains, or that there is a strict structural isomorphism (parallel laws) between the material and soul realms? This affects whether LawOfNatureInSoul should be a distinct class or share instances with LawOfNatureInMatter.

Should the concrete instantiation of LawOfNature in matter be modeled with BFO_0000050 (part-of), or with a concretization relation (OBI or RO)? BFO_0000050 may not be the most precise predicate here.
Is 'form' here synonymous with 'soul' (as in Leibnizian substantial forms), or is it a broader category that includes non-minded forms?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that there are laws of nature operative in matter and analogous (like) laws operative in souls or forms. I model LawOfNature as a new class under BFO_0000031 (generically dependent continuant), since laws of nature function as abstract patterns or principles that can be concretely instantiated in different substrates—analogous to how a software program or a mathematical structure is a GDC. Two subclasses are minted: LawOfNatureInMatter (instantiated in NaturalMaterialEntity) and LawOfNatureInSoul (instantiated in SimpleSubstance/Soul). The relations to matter and soul are tentative and flagged in open_questions, since BFO lacks a native 'concretely instantiated in' predicate at the class level, and the correct predicate for this dependency is uncertain. The key philosophical question—whether laws are dispositions (BFO_0000016) or abstract patterns (BFO_0000031)—is also raised for user clarification.

proposal.utterance: Efforts properly exist only in substances themselves, not in other entities.

entities.label: Effort
entities.rationale: An 'effort' in the Leibnizian sense (conatus) is an intrinsic, internally-grounded tendency or striving belonging to a substance. This maps best to BFO Disposition (BFO_0000016), which is a specifically dependent continuant that is internally grounded in its bearer and represents a tendency or capacity to act. It is a class because the utterance speaks generically of efforts.

entities.label: EffortSubstanceInherence
entities.rationale: The ontological constraint that Effort inheres only in substances (IndivisibleSubstance / SimpleSubstance) and not in other entity types is itself a formal restriction. We represent this as a universal restriction axiom via a relation rather than a separate class, but we flag it here for the open_questions. Reconsidering: this is better expressed as an OWL restriction on the Effort class (Effort rdfs:subClassOf RO_0000052 only IndivisibleSubstance), not a new entity. Removing from entities; captured in relations.

relations.rationale: Effort is typed as a subclass of Disposition (BFO_0000016), the appropriate BFO type for intrinsic, internally-grounded tendencies that are specifically dependent on their bearer.

Effort as a striving within a substance is closely related to SubstanceProgress (already in the ontology as a Disposition); alternatively Effort may be a sibling or subclass of SubstanceProgress depending on user intent. Flagged in open_questions.

The utterance states that efforts exist (inhere) only in substances themselves. Representing this as 'inheres in' (RO_0000052) pointing to IndivisibleSubstance encodes the restriction that Effort bearers must be substances. In OWL this would be a universal restriction: Effort rdfs:subClassOf (RO_0000052 only IndivisibleSubstance).

open_questions: Should 'Effort' (conatus) be modeled as a subclass of the existing 'SubstanceProgress' (also a Disposition), or as a sibling class directly under BFO_0000016? The two concepts are related but SubstanceProgress may already cover this.

Should the bearer restriction be expressed as an OWL universal restriction (Effort subClassOf RO_0000052 only IndivisibleSubstance) to formally block Effort from inhering in non-substances, or is a weaker assertion sufficient?
Does 'substance' here refer specifically to 'IndivisibleSubstance' or 'SimpleSubstance' in the existing ontology, or to a broader notion? This affects which class serves as the bearer.

Is this utterance drawing from Leibniz's notion of conatus as a primitive striving, or from another philosophical tradition? The answer may affect how we distinguish Effort from ActiveForce already in the ontology.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that 'efforts' (conatus-like strivings) are ontologically restricted to inhere exclusively in substances and cannot exist in other kinds of entities. In BFO terms, this is best captured by introducing a new class 'Effort' typed as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) — an internally-grounded, specifically dependent continuant — with a universal restriction that its bearer must be an IndivisibleSubstance. The second proposed entity (EffortSubstanceInherence) was reconsidered and collapsed into the relation, since the restriction is best expressed as an OWL axiom rather than a separate entity. The key open questions concern whether Effort should be a subclass of the existing SubstanceProgress disposition, how to distinguish it from the existing individual ActiveForce, and exactly which existing substance class serves as the bearer.

proposal.utterance: The same quantity of moving force is always preserved in bodies.

entities.label: MovingForce
entities.rationale: Moving force (vis viva / motive force) is a measurable property inhering in bodies — a quality in BFO terms. It is distinct from the already-existing ActiveForce individual, which is a specific Leibnizian metaphysical posit; here we need a class representing the kind of quantity that is conserved.

entities.label: ConservationOfMovingForce
entities.rationale: The claim that the same quantity of moving force is always preserved is a law or principle — an information artifact / generically dependent continuant that can be instantiated in multiple physical systems. It is analogous to the already-existing ForceMeasurementPrinciple individual.

entities.label: QuantityConservation
entities.rationale: The invariance (sameness) of quantity across time is a quality — specifically a kind of equality-over-time — inhering in the aggregate of bodies. This generalises the existing Equality class and can serve as its parent or sibling.

relations.rationale: Conservation of a quantity is a species of equality (the quantity is equal across temporal intervals), so QuantityConservation subclasses Equality.
The conservation principle is an individual generically dependent continuant (a physical law / information content entity).

The conservation-of-moving-force claim is part of (or at least closely related to) the broader ForceMeasurementPrinciple already in the ontology; representing it as a part captures Leibniz's view that conservation follows from the correct measure of force.

open_questions: Should MovingForce be modeled as a subclass of an existing quality (e.g. MotionQuality) rather than a direct subclass of BFO Quality?
Is 'ConservationOfMovingForce' better treated as a part of ForceMeasurementPrinciple, or as a distinct co-equal principle alongside it?

Should 'bodies' (the bearers of moving force) be represented as an explicit class (e.g. ExtendedBody) distinct from the existing Body individual, given that this claim is universal over all material bodies?
Does 'quantity' here refer to Leibniz's mv² (vis viva) specifically, or to a more general notion of motive force? This affects whether MovingForce should be further specialised.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts Leibniz's conservation law: the total quantity of moving force in all bodies is invariant. This introduces three ontological commitments: (1) MovingForce, a quality-kind inhering in material bodies; (2) QuantityConservation, a quality-kind capturing the invariance (equality over time) of such a quantity, modelled as a subclass of the existing Equality class; and (3) ConservationOfMovingForce, an individual law/principle (generically dependent continuant) that encodes this claim and stands as a part of the existing ForceMeasurementPrinciple. No new processes are asserted; the statement is a nomological claim, not a report of a particular happening.

proposal.utterance: There exists a law of nature concerning the preservation of direction across bodies.

entities.label: Law of Conservation of Direction
entities.rationale: A law of nature is a propositional content — a pattern or rule that can be instantiated in multiple bearers and copied; it is not itself a material thing nor a process. BFO_0000031 (generically dependent continuant) best captures a natural law as informational/propositional content. This parallels the existing RuleOfMotion and RuleOfRest individuals already in the ontology.

relations.rationale: Asserts the individual as a generically dependent continuant, consistent with the treatment of RuleOfMotion and RuleOfRest.

open_questions: Is this law intended to be a sub-kind of the existing RuleOfMotion individual or a sibling alongside it? Should we introduce a class 'LawOfNature' (subclass of BFO_0000031) under which RuleOfMotion, RuleOfRest, and LawOfConservationOfDirection are all typed?

Does 'preservation of direction across bodies' refer specifically to Descartes' second rule of nature (conservation of rectilinear motion/direction), or is it a more general principle? This affects whether it should be identified with or related to the existing RuleOfMotion individual.
Should this law be related to the existing RuleOfMotion or RuleOfRest individuals via a part-of or sibling relation?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts the existence of a natural law concerning the conservation of direction when motion is transferred between bodies. Natural laws are best modeled in BFO as generically dependent continuants (BFO_0000031) — they are propositional/informational patterns that can in principle be instantiated or copied across contexts. This is consistent with how RuleOfMotion and RuleOfRest are already represented in the ontology. I mint a new individual 'LawOfConservationOfDirection' typed as BFO_0000031. No new class is minted yet, though I flag the open question of whether a 'LawOfNature' class should be introduced to subsume these individuals. No process or quality is asserted, as the utterance is about the existence of the law itself, not any particular physical occurrence.

proposal.utterance: Pre-established harmony is the correct means by which soul and body communicate.

entities.label: Pre-Established Harmony
entities.rationale: Pre-established harmony is Leibniz's doctrine that soul and body are coordinated through a divinely instituted disposition/capacity built into each substance from creation, not through causal interaction. It is internally grounded in the natures of substances, making Disposition (BFO_0000016) the best fit. It is an individual (a specific metaphysical principle posited as uniquely actual), not a class.

entities.label: SoulBodyCommunication
entities.rationale: The communication between soul and body (the coordinated unfolding of mental and physical states) is a kind of process — an occurrent. Typing it as a class under MentalChange captures the dynamic, temporal character of the coordination.

relations.rationale: PreEstablishedHarmony is an individual disposition, internally grounded in the nature of substances.
Pre-established harmony is realized in the process of soul-body communication; BFO_0000054 (realized in) links a realizable entity to the process in which it manifests.
The disposition of pre-established harmony inheres in the Soul (and correlatively in the Body), grounding the coordination from the soul's side.
Pre-established harmony also inheres in Body, since both soul and body bear the coordinated dispositions that constitute the harmony.
Soul-body communication is a subclass of MentalChange, capturing the occurrent coordination between mental and physical states.
Soul participates in the process of soul-body communication.
Body participates in the process of soul-body communication.

open_questions: Should PreEstablishedHarmony be modeled as a class (a general kind of harmony) rather than an individual, since Leibniz applies it universally to all soul-body pairs and to all substances in the universe?
Should SoulBodyCommunication be typed as a subclass of LegalProcess or left under MentalChange? (MentalChange seems more appropriate for Leibniz's metaphysical context.)
The utterance asserts this is the 'correct' means — should a truth-value or epistemic status quality be added to capture the normative/assertoric force, or is that outside ontological scope?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that pre-established harmony is the mechanism (means) by which soul and body communicate. This introduces two new ontological commitments: (1) Pre-Established Harmony as an individual disposition (BFO_0000016) that inheres in both Soul and Body — it is internally grounded in the natures of those substances, aligning with Disposition rather than Role; and (2) SoulBodyCommunication as a process class (BFO_0000015) in which that disposition is realized. The disposition is linked to Soul and Body via RO_0000052 (inheres in), and to the communication process via BFO_0000054 (realized in). Both Soul and Body are existing individuals. The word 'correct' expresses an epistemic or normative claim that does not add a new entity but could be noted as an open question about assertoric modeling.

proposal.utterance: God made soul and body such that each follows its own laws while according with the other.

entities.label: PsychophysicalAccord
entities.rationale: The accord between soul and body — each following its own laws while harmonizing with the other — is a quality of the Soul-Body system, analogous to PerfectMutualAccord already in the ontology but more specifically the psychophysical variant Leibniz describes. However, PerfectMutualAccord already exists and may be reusable; see open questions.

entities.label: SoulLaw
entities.rationale: The law governing the soul's operations is an information-like pattern (a generically dependent continuant) — a principle that specifies how the soul proceeds through its changes, akin to RuleOfMotion/RuleOfRest but for soul.

entities.label: BodyLaw
entities.rationale: The law governing the body's operations is likewise an information-like pattern specifying how the body proceeds mechanically, parallel to SoulLaw.

entities.label: DivineCreationOfHarmony
entities.rationale: God's act of making soul and body such that they accord is a process (a divine act/creation event). This is distinct from the ongoing DivineOrdering — it is the specific founding act of establishing the pre-established harmony between soul and body.

relations.rationale: God participates in (as agent of) the DivineCreationOfHarmony process; God is a participant.
Soul participates in the DivineCreationOfHarmony as a product/object of the creation.
Body participates in the DivineCreationOfHarmony as a product/object of the creation.
The law of the soul is part of (specifically dependent on) the soul-body system; expressed loosely as part-of the union context. Open to revision — see open questions.
The law of the body is similarly part of the soul-body system.
The PerfectMutualAccord (the pre-established harmony between soul and body) inheres in the SoulBodyUnion as a quality of that composite.
The specific act of creating psychophysical harmony is part of the broader DivineOrdering process.

open_questions: Is PerfectMutualAccord (already in the ontology) sufficient to represent the soul-body accord described here, or does the utterance warrant a distinct individual (e.g., PreEstablishedHarmony) to distinguish it from a more general notion of mutual accord?

Should SoulLaw and BodyLaw be typed as classes (kinds of laws) rather than individuals, since Leibniz discusses them generically? Or are they best treated as the specific laws of these particular individuals?

The relation between SoulLaw/BodyLaw and Soul/Body should arguably be expressed as the law being 'about' or 'governing' Soul/Body — BFO lacks a direct 'governs' predicate. Should we mint a working:governs relation, or use BFO_0000050 (part-of) loosely?
Is DivineCreationOfHarmony the same event as the existing Creation individual, or is it a sub-event? Should it be typed as a subclass of Creation?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts Leibniz's doctrine of pre-established harmony: God created soul and body so that each follows its own intrinsic laws (soul's mental/perceptual laws; body's mechanical laws) while nevertheless according perfectly with the other. Four ontological commitments are identified: (1) there is a divine founding process (DivineCreationOfHarmony) in which God established this arrangement — modeled as a Process (BFO_0000015) with God, Soul, and Body as participants; (2) there is a law governing soul's operations (SoulLaw) and (3) a law governing body's operations (BodyLaw), both modeled as generically dependent continuants (BFO_0000031) since they are information-like patterns/rules; and (4) the resulting accord between soul and body is captured by the already-existing PerfectMutualAccord individual, which is now asserted to inhere in SoulBodyUnion. The existing individuals God, Soul, Body, SoulBodyUnion, and DivineOrdering are reused. RuleOfMotion/RuleOfRest are analogous but distinct (they govern Nature generally); SoulLaw and BodyLaw are the psychophysical-domain parallels.

proposal.utterance: The soul and body have real independence.

entities.label: RealIndependence
entities.rationale: Real independence is a property (quality) that can inhere in a substance. It is a measurable/ascribable characteristic rather than a role or disposition — it describes an intrinsic relational status of the bearer.

entities.label: SoulRealIndependence
entities.rationale: This is the specific instance of RealIndependence inhering in the Soul individual.

entities.label: BodyRealIndependence
entities.rationale: This is the specific instance of RealIndependence inhering in the Body individual.

relations.rationale: SoulRealIndependence is an instance of the RealIndependence quality class.
BodyRealIndependence is an instance of the RealIndependence quality class.
The quality of real independence inheres in Soul (BFO: SDC inheres in its bearer).
The quality of real independence inheres in Body (BFO: SDC inheres in its bearer).
Soul bears the quality SoulRealIndependence.
Body bears the quality BodyRealIndependence.

open_questions: Is 'real independence' here meant in the Leibnizian/Cartesian metaphysical sense (that soul and body are each complete substances, not dependent on one another for existence), or does it refer to some functional/causal independence? This affects whether it is better modeled as a Quality, a Disposition, or even a Role.
Should RealIndependence be related to the existing working:RealUnity class, since both concern the metaphysical status of substances?
Is this independence mutual (each from the other) or absolute (from all other things)? If mutual, a relational quality or a BFO relational property might be more appropriate.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that Soul and Body each possess real independence. In BFO, a property that characterizes a particular individual and inheres in it is a specifically dependent continuant — most naturally a Quality (BFO_0000019), since independence here is an intrinsic metaphysical characteristic rather than a capacity to act (Disposition) or an externally-conferred function (Role). I mint a new class RealIndependence as a subclass of Quality, and create two individuals — SoulRealIndependence and BodyRealIndependence — as instances of that class inhering in the already-existing Soul and Body individuals via RO_0000052 (inheres in) / RO_0000053 (bearer of). No new individuals for Soul or Body are needed. An open question is raised about whether the concept is better modeled as a Disposition, given that some philosophers treat substance-independence as a kind of modal capacity.

proposal.utterance: Soul and body achieve harmony through pre-established agreement by divine contrivance.

entities.label: PreEstablishedHarmony
entities.rationale: The pre-established harmony is a specific relational quality that inheres in the Soul-Body union as a whole — it is an intrinsic property of their coordinated state, not a process or a document. It is distinct from PerfectMutualAccord (which is a cosmic quality of the universe's substances) in that it specifically concerns the Soul-Body dyad. Typed as a Quality (BFO_0000019).

entities.label: DivineContrivance
entities.rationale: The divine contrivance is the act by which God arranges the pre-established harmony — it is an occurrent, a process performed by the divine agent. entities.rationale: The axiom of identity (A=A) is a specific logical/propositional content — a generically dependent continuant (an informational entity that can be encoded in multiple bearers). It is a named individual because it is the specific logical principle, not merely a kind.

entities.label: AxiomOfContradiction
entities.rationale: The axiom of contradiction (not both A and not-A) is likewise a specific named logical principle — a generically dependent continuant. It is a canonical individual axiom in Leibniz's system.

I model 'PrimitiveEpistemicPrinciple' as a new class under BFO generically dependent continuant (BFO_0000031) since principles are propositional/informational contents. entities.label: Truth
entities.rationale: Truths as propositional contents are information structures that can be instantiated in multiple bearers; modeled as a subclass of Generically Dependent Continuant (GDC), analogous to how Idea and Thought are already typed.

entities.label: PrimitivePrinciple

entities.rationale: A derived truth is any truth other than a primitive principle; it is capable of proof. Modeled as a subtype of Truth (GDC), disjoint from PrimitivePrinciple.

entities.label: Provability
entities.rationale: Provability is the capacity of a truth to be demonstrated from prior truths; it is intrinsically grounded in the content of the truth and is therefore a Disposition (internally grounded realizable entity).

entities.label: Proof
entities.rationale: A proof is the process through which a derived truth is demonstrated; it is a temporal unfolding and therefore a Process (Occurrent).

relations.rationale: Every derived truth is a kind of truth.

Provability is a disposition inhering in derived truths.
The disposition Provability inheres in instances of DerivedTruth (every non-primitive truth has the capacity to be proved).
The disposition Provability is realized in the process of Proof.

proposal.utterance: The absolute has influence upon compound things because they result from the limitation of the absolute.

entities.label: Absolute
entities.rationale: The 'absolute' here functions as a unique, ontologically primitive entity — the ultimate source from which compound things result. It is modeled as an individual material entity (consistent with how God/NecessaryBeing are modeled in this ontology). It could alternately be identified with working:God or working:NecessaryBeing; see open_questions.

entities.label: CompoundThing
entities.rationale: Compound things are composite material entities that result from limitation of the absolute. They are a natural class of material entities (contrasted with simple/indivisible substances already in the ontology).

entities.label: Limitation
entities.rationale: Limitation is a quality that inheres in compound things — it is the property by which they are bounded or restricted versions of the absolute. It is a specifically dependent continuant that qualifies the compound thing.

entities.label: AbsoluteInfluence
entities.rationale: The absolute's influence on compound things is an internally grounded capacity of the absolute — a disposition to causally affect compound things. Modeled as a disposition (BFO_0000016) inhering in the Absolute individual.

relations.rationale: The disposition of influence inheres in the Absolute as its bearer.
Limitation is a kind of Quality (specifically dependent continuant).
CompoundThing is a subclass of Material entity.
Compound things are natural material entities, consistent with the ontology's existing NaturalMaterialEntity class.

open_questions: Should 'the Absolute' be identified with an existing individual such as working:God or working:NecessaryBeing, or is it a distinct entity in this philosophical context (e.g., Spinoza's Substance, Leibniz's God, or another tradition)?

Is 'Limitation' here a quality of compound things (they are limited), or a process by which the absolute produces compound things? If it is a productive process (not merely a quality), it should be typed as BFO_0000015 (Process) rather than BFO_0000019 (Quality).
Should 'AbsoluteInfluence' be a disposition (BFO_0000016) or a role (BFO_0000023)? If the influence is externally grounded by the existence of compound things, a role may be more appropriate.
What is the philosophical tradition/author being modeled? This affects whether 'absolute' maps to God, Substance, the One, etc.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts three ontological claims: (1) there exists an Absolute entity; (2) there exist compound things; (3) the Absolute has influence over compound things because they result from its limitation. I model the Absolute as a new individual of type BFO_0000040, pending clarification about whether it should be identified with existing individuals (God, NecessaryBeing). CompoundThing is introduced as a new class of material entities (subclass of NaturalMaterialEntity), contrasting with the existing SimpleSubstance/IndivisibleSubstance classes. Limitation is modeled as a Quality class (BFO_0000019) that inheres in compound things, capturing the notion that they are bounded or restricted versions of the absolute — though if limitation is understood as a generative process, it should be retyped as BFO_0000015. AbsoluteInfluence is modeled as a disposition inhering in the Absolute, since it is an internally grounded causal capacity. Key open questions concern the philosophical tradition and whether existing individuals can be reused.

entities.rationale: The positive idea of the infinite is a specific cognitive content — an idea in the Leibnizian/Cartesian sense — best typed as a generically dependent continuant (an informational/conceptual pattern) and an instance of the existing working:Idea class.

entities.label: IdeaOfFinite

proposal.utterance: We know our own existence by immediate intuition.

entities.label: ImmediateIntuition
entities.rationale: Immediate intuition is a mental process or act by which a mind apprehends something directly — a sub-kind of MentalChange (itself a Process). It is a kind rather than an individual because the claim is general.

entities.label: SelfKnowledge
entities.rationale: Knowledge of one's own existence is informational content — a generically dependent continuant that can be instantiated in a mind. It is a sub-kind of Idea (already in the ontology as a GDC). Modeled as a class because the assertion is generic.

entities.label: OwnExistence
entities.rationale: One's own existence — the fact of existing — is best captured as a quality (specifically a mode of being) inhering in the bearer (the soul/mind). It is a new class capturing the object of the intuition.

relations.rationale: Self-knowledge is a species of Idea (GDC) already in the ontology.
Immediate intuition is a mental change/process, sub-kind of MentalChange.

The process of immediate intuition realizes (produces/bears) self-knowledge as its output content — using 'realizes' loosely; strictly BFO_0000055 goes from process to realizable, but here it captures that intuition is the act through which self-knowledge is actualized. Flag for open question.

open_questions: In Leibniz's context, is 'immediate intuition of one's own existence' an epistemological claim about the soul knowing itself, or a metaphysical claim about existence being self-evident? This affects whether SelfKnowledge should be a Disposition (capacity to know oneself) rather than a GDC.

Should ImmediateIntuition be typed as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) — the capacity for direct self-apprehension — rather than a Process, given that Leibniz may intend it as a permanent faculty rather than a single occurrence?

Should we instead use a custom 'produces' or 'has_output' relation, or type SelfKnowledge as a Disposition that is realized in the intuition process?

This introduces three new ontological items: (1) ImmediateIntuition as a sub-kind of MentalChange (a direct, non-inferential mental process), (2) SelfKnowledge as a sub-kind of Idea (the informational content — one's grasp of one's own existence — that results), and (3) OwnExistence as a Quality inhering in the soul (the object that is known). The Soul individual already exists in the ontology as the bearer. The key interpretive uncertainty is whether 'intuition' here is a process-token or a standing capacity (disposition), and whether the BFO_0000055 'realizes' relation adequately captures the link between the intuiting process and the knowledge content produced. Ontologically this introduces (1) MassOfMatter as a class of NaturalMaterialEntity, (2) Perception as a Disposition that parts may or may not bear, (3) PerceptionlessPartConstraint as the dispositional state characterising a mass whose parts all lack Perception, (4) ThinkingCapacity as the Disposition constitutive of a 'thinking whole', and (5) ThinkingWhole as a subclass of MassOfMatter that bears ThinkingCapacity. entities.label: Space
entities.rationale: Space as a kind of immaterial entity (spatial region or site in BFO terms); typed as a class since the utterance speaks generically about space.

entities.label: Time
entities.rationale: Time as a kind of temporal region in BFO; the utterance asserts something about time generically.

entities.label: Number
entities.rationale: A number is an abstract informational/mathematical entity; best typed as a generically dependent continuant (a pattern or information structure that can be concretized in multiple bearers).

entities.label: Infinity
entities.rationale: Infinity (or being-infinite) is a quality that could in principle inhere in a quantity or magnitude; the utterance denies that Space, Time, or Number bears this quality.

open_questions: The utterance is a negative existential claim (no space/time/number is infinite). BFO-grounded graphs represent positive assertions; should we represent this denial explicitly via a disjointness or negation axiom (e.g., Space disjointWith BearerOfInfinity), or is it sufficient to simply record the relevant classes and note the denial in an annotation?
Is 'Number' here meant in a mathematical/abstract sense (GDC) or as a quantity quality (BFO_0000019)? The choice affects how 'infinity' as a quality can inhere in it.
Is this claim from a specific philosophical source (e.g., Leibniz, Descartes) so we can annotate provenance appropriately?
Should 'Infinity' be modeled as a Quality (inhering in a bearer) or as a Disposition (a capacity to be unbounded)? The former seems more appropriate but the user's intent should confirm.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance 'There is no space, time, or number which is infinite' introduces three generic kinds—Space, Time, and Number—and the property of being Infinite (Infinity). Space is modeled as a subclass of BFO Immaterial Entity, Time as a subclass of Temporal Region, and Number as a Generically Dependent Continuant (abstract pattern). Infinity is proposed as a Quality class. Crucially, the utterance is a universal negative claim: no instance of Space, Time, or Number bears the quality Infinity. BFO itself has no built-in negation constructor, so the ontological commitment here is primarily to the four classes; the denial would need to be expressed as a disjointness or closed-world annotation axiom, which is flagged as an open question. No relations are asserted positively; the main content is the new class vocabulary. No existing individuals or classes in the working ontology need to be reused.

proposal.utterance: In addition to the world of finite things, there exists a unique Being who governs the universe.

entities.label: God
entities.rationale: God already exists as an individual of type BFO_0000040 in the ontology; reusing it.

entities.label: Universe
entities.rationale: Universe already exists as an individual of type BFO_0000040; reusing it to represent 'the world of finite things'.

entities.label: GovernanceRole
entities.rationale: The utterance asserts that God governs the universe. Governance is an externally grounded social/functional role borne by God with respect to the universe. Modeled as a subclass of Role (BFO_0000023). It could also be a subclass of the existing LegalRole but more broadly it is just a Role; we place it under BFO_0000023 directly with LegalRole as a sibling, not parent, unless the user prefers otherwise.

entities.label: GodGovernanceRole
entities.rationale: The specific instance of GovernanceRole inhering in God with respect to the Universe.

entities.label: Uniqueness
entities.rationale: The utterance explicitly asserts God is a 'unique Being', which is a quality of being one-of-a-kind. Modeled as a Quality class.

entities.label: GodUniqueness
entities.rationale: The specific Uniqueness quality inhering in God.

relations.rationale: GodGovernanceRole is an instance of GovernanceRole.
GovernanceRole is a kind of Role in BFO.
God bears the GodGovernanceRole, as it governs the universe.
GodGovernanceRole inheres in God.
GodUniqueness is an instance of Uniqueness.
Uniqueness is a kind of Quality.
God bears the quality of uniqueness.
GodUniqueness inheres in God.
The universe participates in DivineOrdering (already in ontology), which represents God's governing activity over it.

open_questions: Should GovernanceRole be a subclass of the existing LegalRole, or should it be a direct subclass of BFO_0000023 (Role) as a broader, non-legal governance role? The utterance does not imply a legal context.
The existing individual DivineOrdering (type BFO_0000015, Process) already partially captures divine governance. Should GodGovernanceRole be realized in DivineOrdering via BFO_0000054 (realized in)?

Is 'uniqueness' here intended as numerical uniqueness (there is only one such being) or qualitative perfection? This affects whether Uniqueness is best modeled as a Quality (BFO_0000019) or as something else.

Should 'the world of finite things' (Universe) be formally distinguished from God as a separate ontological realm, or is the Universe simply asserted to be governed by God (already captured by existing individuals)?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance makes two main ontological commitments: (1) there is a unique Being distinct from finite things who governs the universe, and (2) this being governs the universe. God and Universe already exist as individuals in the ontology. The governance relation is new and is modeled via a new GovernanceRole class (subclass of BFO_0000023 Role) with an instance GodGovernanceRole inhering in God. The existing DivineOrdering process can serve as the realization of this governance role. Uniqueness is modeled as a new Quality class with an instance GodUniqueness inhering in God, capturing the 'unique Being' assertion. Several open questions remain about the precise sub-classification of GovernanceRole and the interpretation of uniqueness.

proposal.utterance: This unique Being creates and fashions the world and is superior to and distinct from it.

entities.label: Creation
entities.rationale: Creation already exists in the ontology as a Process class; reusing it.

entities.label: WorldFashioning
entities.rationale: Fashioning the world is a distinct creative/formative process (demiurgic shaping, ordering) beyond bare creation ex nihilo; merits its own Process class.

entities.label: World
entities.rationale: The world that is created and fashioned is a concrete material individual (cf. existing Universe individual, but 'world' may be more specific in some Leibnizian senses; minting a distinct individual pending user confirmation). Could alternatively be identified with Universe.

entities.label: Transcendence
entities.rationale: God's being superior to and distinct from the world is a quality (a relational quality of superiority/non-identity) inhering in God. Modeled as an individual quality inhering in God.

relations.rationale: God (the unique Being) participates in the Creation process as its agent/initiator.
God participates in the WorldFashioning process, actively shaping/ordering the world.
The Creation process has the World as its output participant.
The WorldFashioning process has the World as its object participant.
The quality of Transcendence (superiority to and distinctness from the world) inheres in God.

open_questions: Should 'World' be identified with the existing individual 'Universe' (working:Universe), or does the source text treat them as distinct (e.g., Universe = totality of created things, World = the fashioned/ordered creation)?

Is 'Transcendence' better typed as a Quality (BFO_0000019) or as a Role (BFO_0000023)? Since superiority/distinctness is an intrinsic property of the unique Being rather than externally conferred, Quality seems preferable, but please confirm.
Does 'fashions' imply a teleological/demiurgic ordering process distinct from creation ex nihilo, or should both be collapsed into the existing 'Creation' class?
Is the 'unique Being' explicitly identified with the existing individual 'God' (working:God), or is a new individual needed (e.g., a Leibnizian God vs. a different philosophical context)?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts three ontological commitments: (1) a unique Being (identified with existing individual God) creates the world — reusing the existing Creation class as a process in which God participates; (2) God fashions/orders the world — a potentially distinct formative process (WorldFashioning) beyond bare creation; (3) God is superior to and distinct from the world — modeled as a Quality (Transcendence) inhering in God, capturing the relational property of transcendence. The World is minted as a new Material entity individual, though it may be collapsible with the existing Universe individual pending user clarification. All new entities are typed conservatively against BFO. Open questions flag the key ambiguities for human confirmation before committing.

proposal.utterance: There exists a necessary being whose essence is existence.

entities.label: NecessaryBeing
entities.rationale: NecessaryBeing already exists as an individual typed BFO_0000040. Reusing it.

entities.label: EssenceIsExistenceQuality
entities.rationale: The claim 'essence is existence' is a distinctive metaphysical property of the necessary being — the identity of its essence with its act of existing. In BFO terms this is best modeled as a Quality inhering in NecessaryBeing. It is not a disposition (no triggering condition) nor a role (not externally grounded), so Quality is the most conservative choice.

relations.rationale: The quality 'essence is existence' inheres in the NecessaryBeing as its bearer, per BFO SDC-bearer relation RO_0000052 (inheres in).
Inverse: NecessaryBeing bears the EssenceIsExistenceQuality, per RO_0000053 (bearer of).

open_questions: Should 'essence is existence' be modeled as a Quality (a static property) or as a Disposition (a capacity grounding existence at every moment)? Leibniz/Aquinas-style readings might prefer Disposition (BFO_0000016) to capture the 'active self-grounding' sense.

Is NecessaryBeing intended to be the same individual as 'God' already in the ontology? If so, we may want to assert working:NecessaryBeing = working:God (owl:sameAs) rather than keeping two individuals.
Should 'existence' be represented as a separate Quality or Process individual to which EssenceIsExistenceQuality refers, or is the current single-quality representation sufficient?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that there exists a necessary being (already modeled as the individual working:NecessaryBeing : BFO_0000040) and that its essence is identical with its existence. BFO does not have a native 'essence' category; the closest conservative mapping for a constitutive, non-dispositional, non-role metaphysical property is Quality (BFO_0000019). Accordingly, a new individual EssenceIsExistenceQuality is minted as a Quality that inheres in NecessaryBeing via RO_0000052/RO_0000053. The identity claim (essence = existence) is encoded in the label and can be elaborated with an annotation. Three open questions are raised: whether Disposition better captures the active self-grounding reading, whether NecessaryBeing should be declared owl:sameAs God, and whether existence itself warrants a separate node.
