proposal.utterance: The world is not metaphysically necessary, only physically or hypothetically necessary.

entities.label: MetaphysicalNecessity
entities.rationale: Metaphysical necessity is a modal property — an intrinsic, internally grounded constraint on what can or cannot be otherwise. BFO_0000016 (Disposition) captures internally grounded capacities/constraints that may or may not be realized. This models 'necessity' as a dispositional quality of a bearer (e.g., God vs. the world).

entities.label: PhysicalNecessity
entities.rationale: Physical (hypothetical) necessity is an externally grounded, law-constrained disposition — the world could have been otherwise, but given the laws God chose, it proceeds necessarily. Modeled as a subtype of Disposition distinct from MetaphysicalNecessity.

entities.label: HypotheticalNecessity
entities.rationale: Hypothetical necessity is the same modality as physical necessity in Leibniz: necessity conditional on God's free choice of this world. Modeled as a subclass of PhysicalNecessity to capture the synonymy while allowing distinction if needed.

entities.label: WorldMetaphysicalNecessity
entities.rationale: The claim is that the world lacks metaphysical necessity — i.e., it does not bear a MetaphysicalNecessity disposition. Representing this as a named individual of type MetaphysicalNecessity would be incorrect (it lacks it). Instead we assert the absence via an open question, but we can still mint a quality node representing the modal status of the world as physically/hypothetically necessary.

entities.label: WorldPhysicalNecessity
entities.rationale: The specific disposition of physical/hypothetical necessity that inheres in the Universe individual, representing the claim that the world IS physically necessary.

relations.rationale: PhysicalNecessity is a subtype of the broader necessity class hierarchy — allowing us to assert via negation that the world lacks the top-level metaphysical necessity while bearing only the weaker physical subtype.
Hypothetical necessity is treated as equivalent to or a species of physical necessity in this Leibnizian context.
The world's modal status is an instance of PhysicalNecessity.
The disposition of physical necessity inheres in the Universe individual.
Universe bears the physical necessity disposition.

open_questions: Should MetaphysicalNecessity be modeled as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) or a Quality (BFO_0000019)? Dispositions are internally grounded tendencies that may or may not be realized; qualities are always fully present. Necessity as a modal property seems closer to a disposition, but the user may prefer Quality for metaphysical status.

How should we formally represent the ABSENCE of metaphysical necessity in the Universe? OWL can express this via a negative property assertion or a disjointness axiom (e.g., Universe is disjoint from bearers of MetaphysicalNecessity). Should we add such a constraint?
Should HypotheticalNecessity be a strict subclass of PhysicalNecessity, or should they be asserted as equivalent classes (owl:equivalentClass)?
Is the 'world' here the same individual as working:Universe already in the ontology, or does it refer to a distinct concept (e.g., the created order distinct from God's necessary being)?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts a Leibnizian modal distinction: the world (Universe) lacks metaphysical necessity (which belongs only to God as NecessaryBeing) but possesses physical or hypothetical necessity — necessity conditional on God's free choice of the best possible world. I mint three new classes under Disposition: MetaphysicalNecessity, PhysicalNecessity (subclass), and HypotheticalNecessity (subclass of PhysicalNecessity, treated as synonymous in this context). I also mint two individuals: WorldPhysicalNecessity as a disposition instance that inheres in Universe, and WorldMetaphysicalNecessity is discussed but not asserted as inhering (the claim is a negation). The existing individual NecessaryBeing (typed as BFO_0000040) would be the appropriate bearer of a MetaphysicalNecessity instance, but that positive assertion was not made in this utterance. Key open questions concern whether to model necessity as Quality vs. Disposition, how to formally encode the negation, and whether HypotheticalNecessity should be equivalent to PhysicalNecessity.

proposal.utterance: Possible things have a tendency or inclination toward existence according to their degree of perfection.

entities.label: PossibleThing
entities.rationale: A 'possible thing' is a continuant (something that could persist through time) that is not yet actual. It is most naturally typed as a kind of continuant at the independent continuant level, since the claim concerns things that have or could have existence. Typing under BFO_0000002 (Continuant) keeps it maximally general without prejudging whether it is material or immaterial.

entities.label: TendencyTowardExistence
entities.rationale: A tendency or inclination toward existence is internally grounded in the bearer (the possible thing) and is directed toward a realizable outcome (coming into existence). This maps naturally to BFO Disposition. It is analogous to existing working class Potentiality but is specifically directed toward existence per se.

entities.label: DegreeOfPerfection
entities.rationale: Degree of perfection is a measurable scalar property inhering in a possible thing; it determines the magnitude of the tendency toward existence. Quality is the appropriate BFO type for a measurable/gradable property of a bearer.

relations.rationale: TendencyTowardExistence is a specific kind of Potentiality (already in the ontology), specialised toward existence rather than other outcomes.
The tendency inheres in the possible thing (disposition inheres in its bearer per BFO).
The degree of perfection is a quality inhering in the possible thing.

open_questions: Should PossibleThing be typed under BFO_0000002 (Continuant) rather than BFO_0000040 (Material entity), to remain neutral about whether possible things are material or immaterial? The claim seems to apply to all possible substances, including immaterial ones like souls.

Is TendencyTowardExistence best modeled as a subclass of the existing working:Potentiality, or should it be a sibling disposition class? The Leibnizian claim may intend it as a sui generis striving (conatus) distinct from mere potentiality.

Does 'degree of perfection' here map to a scalar BFO Quality (e.g., a ratio scale), or should it be modeled as a relation between possible things (a partial order)? This affects whether DegreeOfPerfection should also carry a magnitude role.

Should there be an explicit relation (e.g., a custom 'determines-magnitude-of') between DegreeOfPerfection and TendencyTowardExistence to capture that the degree of perfection determines the strength of the tendency?
proposal.rationale_summary: Leibniz's claim that possible things have a tendency toward existence proportional to their degree of perfection introduces three ontological commitments: (1) a class of possible things (continuants not yet actual), (2) a disposition-like tendency toward existence inhering in them, and (3) a quality (degree of perfection) that modulates the magnitude of that tendency. TendencyTowardExistence is typed as a BFO Disposition (internally grounded, directed toward a realizable outcome) and is modeled as a subclass of the existing working:Potentiality since it is a more specific kind of potency. DegreeOfPerfection is typed as a BFO Quality since it is a gradable, measurable property inhering in bearers. PossibleThing is a new class of continuants; its BFO parent is left open pending clarification about material vs. immaterial scope. Relations capture disposition-bearer and quality-bearer dependencies using RO_0000052.

proposal.utterance: Among infinite combinations of possible series, that one exists which brings the most essence or possibility into existence.

entities.label: PossibleSeries
entities.rationale: A 'possible series' is a combinatorial pattern or informational structure — a candidate world-plan or configuration — that can in principle be instantiated or copied. As an abstract combinatorial structure (not yet actualized), it fits best as a generically dependent continuant: a pattern that could be concretized in different ways.

entities.label: ActualSeries

entities.label: IndividualInterestProtection

entities.label: UniversalHarmony
entities.rationale: Universal harmony is a quality of the world/universe — a measurable property of how well its parts cohere. Modeled as a Quality inhering in World.

entities.label: PermittedProtectionConstraint

UniversalHarmony as a quality inheres in the World individual.

The constraint (how much protection is permitted) inheres in the World as a structural feature shaped by universal harmony.

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance makes an axiological claim about universe-level perfection: the universe is not perfect unless individual interests are protected to the maximum extent that universal harmony allows. This introduces three new quality/disposition individuals: UniversePerfection (a quality of the World), UniversalHarmony (a quality of the World), and IndividualInterestProtection (a disposition inhering in the World). These are modeled as inhering in the existing individual World (BFO_0000040). The relation between IndividualInterestProtection and UniversePerfection is rendered via BFO part-of (protection is part of what constitutes perfection). The existing individual IndividualityProtection may overlap with IndividualInterestProtection and is flagged as an open question.

proposal.utterance: Souls bear the relation of citizens to a prince toward God.

entities.label: CitizenRole
entities.rationale: A citizen is a social/political role borne by an individual relative to a governing authority; modeled as a subclass of LegalRole (which is itself a subclass of BFO Role).

entities.label: SubjectToPrinceRole
entities.rationale: Leibniz's analogy specifies the citizen-to-prince relationship as the relational structure; SubjectToPrinceRole captures this more specific political role that souls bear toward God.

entities.label: SoulCitizenRole
entities.rationale: The specific role instance borne by Soul toward God, as asserted in this utterance.

entities.label: PrinceRole
entities.rationale: A prince (sovereign ruler) bears a governance role; this is the correlative role to CitizenRole in the political analogy.

relations.rationale: The citizen role inheres in (is borne by) Soul, per BFO SDC axiom that roles inhere in their bearer.
Inverse: Soul bears the SoulCitizenRole.
God already bears GodGovernanceRole (existing individual); the PrinceRole analogy maps to this existing governance role, so we link GodGovernanceRole (existing) as inhering in God.

GodGovernanceRole is typed as an instance; to capture the analogy, PrinceRole is the class whose individual God's governance role is an instance of. Since GodGovernanceRole is an individual, we assert rdf:type.
God's governance role is an instance of PrinceRole, grounding the prince analogy.

open_questions: Should SoulCitizenRole be a class (with each individual soul bearing an instance) rather than a single individual, given that Leibniz's claim applies to all souls collectively?
Is the 'prince' analogy intended to express only a role/governance relation, or does it also assert a kind of political obligation or disposition (e.g., obedience as a Disposition on souls' part)?
Should we mint a dedicated 'CityOfGodCitizenshipRelation' to formally link SoulCitizenRole to the existing CityOfGod individual (BFO_0000029)?
Does this utterance intend that all souls (as a class) bear this role, or only rational/moral souls specifically?

I mint CitizenRole (a subclass of the existing LegalRole, under BFO Role) and the more specific SubjectToPrinceRole. The concrete role instance SoulCitizenRole inheres in the existing individual Soul and is realized in relation to God. The existing CityOfGod individual (BFO Site) provides the territorial/community context for this polity. proposal.utterance: Souls continue to exist as long as the universe itself.

entities.label: SoulPersistence
entities.rationale: The claim that souls continue to exist as long as the universe is best captured as a disposition (internally grounded capacity/tendency) of the Soul individual — specifically its disposition toward indefinite or co-terminal persistence with the universe. entities.label: UniverseLifetime

relations.rationale: The persistence disposition inheres in the Soul individual.

All three inhere in (are borne by) the existing individual Soul. Using RO_0000053 (bearer of) directly on the Soul individual captures the claim that this particular soul — or souls as a kind — possesses these features. The use of Disposition rather than Quality for (2) and (3) reflects that expression and concentration are active, realizable capacities rather than static measurable properties, consistent with BFO's distinction between Quality and Disposition.

entities.label: Matter
entities.rationale: Matter in Leibniz's sense is the physical, extended substrate — a material entity. Treated as an individual (like Body and World) rather than a class, consistent with the Leibnizian context already in the ontology.

entities.label: Form
entities.rationale: A Leibnizian 'form' is a determinate property or configuration that inheres in matter — best modeled as a Quality class. Not to be confused with EminentForm (an individual already in the ontology representing God's formal content).

entities.label: FormReception
entities.rationale: The successive reception of forms by matter is a temporal unfolding — a process. Modeling 'receives successively' requires a process class in which matter participates and during which forms are realized.

entities.label: Receptivity
entities.rationale: The capacity of matter to receive all forms it is capable of is an internally grounded disposition (not externally conferred), best typed as a Disposition individual inhering in Matter.

relations.rationale: Matter is a natural material entity, consistent with existing NaturalMaterialEntity class.
The disposition of receptivity inheres in Matter as its bearer.
Matter participates in the FormReception process, as the subject that successively receives forms.
The FormReception process realizes the Receptivity disposition of Matter.

I introduce Matter as a new individual of type NaturalMaterialEntity (parallel to Body and World already in the ontology), a Form class as a subclass of Quality (since forms are determinate properties inhering in matter), FormReception as a Process class for the unfolding succession, and Receptivity as a Disposition individual inhering in Matter that is realized in FormReception. Key open questions concern whether Matter should be a class, whether Form should be GDC rather than Quality, and how to handle the explicit temporal succession.

proposal.utterance: Marvels that happen daily are not to be attributed to created intelligences with proportioned wisdom and virtue.

entities.label: DailyMarvel
entities.rationale: A 'marvel that happens daily' is a recurring extraordinary occurrence or process. It is a subtype of Miracle (already in the ontology as a Process subclass), distinguished by its ordinary frequency.

entities.label: CreatedIntelligence
entities.rationale: A 'created intelligence' is a finite mind or intellect brought into existence by a creator (as opposed to the uncreated divine intellect). It is a kind of Mind (already in ontology as BFO_0000040 subclass).

entities.label: ProportionedWisdom
entities.rationale: The 'proportioned wisdom' is a measurable quality of created intelligences — their wisdom is finite and scaled to their nature, contrasted with sovereign wisdom. This is a quality inhering in created intelligences.

entities.label: ProportionedVirtue
entities.rationale: Similarly, 'proportioned virtue' is a finite quality of created intelligences. It is a quality distinct from wisdom but also limited/scaled.

entities.label: AttributionConstraint
entities.rationale: The claim asserts a normative constraint on causal attribution: daily marvels are not attributable to created intelligences. This constraint is a disposition-like property of the explanatory framework — a principle governing causal explanation.

relations.rationale: Daily marvels are a subtype of miracles — extraordinary processes distinguished by their everyday frequency.
Created intelligences are a kind of finite mind, distinct from the divine intellect.
Proportioned wisdom is a quality inhering in created intelligences.
Proportioned virtue is a quality inhering in created intelligences.
The attributive constraint is a disposition-class principle governing how causal responsibility for DailyMarvel processes is assigned — not to CreatedIntelligence bearers.

open_questions: The statement is a normative claim about causal attribution. Should 'AttributionConstraint' be modeled differently — e.g., as a generically dependent continuant (an epistemic or normative rule/proposition) rather than a disposition?
Should 'ProportionedWisdom' and 'ProportionedVirtue' be modeled as subclasses of 'SovereignWisdom' (negations or contrasts), or kept as independent quality subclasses?
Is 'CreatedIntelligence' intended to cover angels and finite rational beings generally, or only human minds? This affects whether it should subclass 'Person' as well as 'Mind'.

The utterance is from Leibniz's Monadology/Discourse context — should the attribution claim be reified as a relation between DailyMarvel and CreatedIntelligence (e.g., a 'not caused by' relation), even though OWL does not natively express negative causation?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that daily marvels — extraordinary processes occurring with ordinary frequency — cannot be causally attributed to created intelligences possessing merely proportioned (finite) wisdom and virtue. This yields four new class-level ontological commitments: (1) DailyMarvel as a subclass of the existing Miracle process class, (2) CreatedIntelligence as a subclass of Mind, (3) ProportionedWisdom and (4) ProportionedVirtue as finite quality classes inhering in created intelligences. Additionally, a fifth class — AttributionConstraint — is proposed as a disposition-class to encode the normative principle that DailyMarvels are not attributable to CreatedIntelligences. The negative causal claim itself cannot be fully expressed in standard OWL without negation constructs, so this is flagged as an open question. All new entities are typed conservatively against BFO 2020.

The Creation class already exists as a process; here the relevant ontological commitment is that God bears the role of maker/craftsman of universal nature. We can capture this via a new role individual borne by God — but we already have AuthorRoleOfGod; see open_questions. Alternatively, the handiwork relation can be modeled as a new individual role or reuse AuthorRoleOfGod.

relations.rationale: God bears the AuthorRoleOfGod; this role is realized in the creation of universal nature. The sentence 'universal nature is the handiwork of God' asserts that God is the author/maker of universal nature, which is captured by God bearing the AuthorRoleOfGod role.
The AuthorRoleOfGod role is realized in the Creation process (already in ontology), which produces UniversalNature. This links the role to the process of making.
UniversalNature participates in (as output/product of) the Creation process — it is what God created, i.e., the handiwork.
Universal nature is typed as a NaturalMaterialEntity individual, the totality of created natural reality.

The existing 'Creation' is typed as a BFO_0000015 Process individual — should it remain a single individual (the one act of creation) or be promoted to a class of creation events?

Is 'handiwork' intended to assert only efficient causation (God as first efficient cause) or also final causation (God as architect with ends)? This affects whether we need additional relations beyond AuthorRoleOfGod and Creation.
Should AuthorRoleOfGod be reused here (it already exists), or do you want a distinct 'CraftsmanRole' or 'MakerRole' to distinguish authorship from craftsmanship?
proposal.rationale_summary: The sentence 'Universal nature is the handiwork of God' makes two key ontological commitments: (1) there is an entity called UniversalNature (the totality of created natural reality, a material entity), and (2) God stands in a productive/authorial relation to it. Rather than minting a new role, I reuse the existing AuthorRoleOfGod individual (already in the ontology as a BFO_0000023 Role borne by God) and the existing Creation process, linking UniversalNature as a participant in that process. UniversalNature is proposed as a new individual typed under NaturalMaterialEntity; however, it may be identical to the existing 'World' individual, which the user should clarify. The core causal/authorial relationship is captured through God bearing AuthorRoleOfGod, realized in Creation, with UniversalNature participating in that creation process.

proposal.utterance: Every natural machine is composed of really infinite organs.

entities.label: NaturalMachine
entities.rationale: A natural machine is a kind of natural material entity (Leibniz's term for organisms and natural bodies). It is a material entity with spatial extent and mass, subclass of existing NaturalMaterialEntity.

entities.label: Organ
entities.rationale: An organ is a material part of a natural machine. Modeled as a subclass of NaturalMaterialEntity, since organs are natural material entities that compose the machine.

entities.label: InfiniteOrganComposition
entities.rationale: The property of being composed of infinitely many organs is a quality inhering in natural machines. It captures Leibniz's claim that natural machines have this structural property.

relations.rationale: NaturalMachine is a kind of NaturalMaterialEntity, inheriting its material nature.
Organs are natural material entities that are parts of natural machines.
Each organ is part of a natural machine (class-level mereological relation expressing composition).
The quality of infinite organ composition inheres in natural machines (class-level: instances of InfiniteOrganComposition inhere in instances of NaturalMachine).

open_questions: Should 'Organ' be typed as a subclass of NaturalMachine as well, given Leibniz's claim that each organ is itself a natural machine? This would make NaturalMachine recursively composed of NaturalMachines.

Should 'infinite' here be represented as a quality (InfiniteOrganComposition as done) or as a cardinality restriction on the part-of relation (OWL minCardinality)? The latter may cause reasoning issues with infinite collections.

Is 'NaturalMachine' the same as or distinct from 'Body' (already an individual in the ontology)? If Body is meant to be the general class of all bodies, should NaturalMachine be a subclass of Body's class instead?
proposal.rationale_summary: Leibniz's assertion that 'every natural machine is composed of really infinite organs' introduces three ontological commitments: (1) the class NaturalMachine as a kind of NaturalMaterialEntity (natural organisms and bodies composed by nature rather than by artifice); (2) the class Organ as the material parts composing natural machines; and (3) InfiniteOrganComposition as a quality inhering in all natural machines, encoding the 'really infinite' structural claim. The part-of relation (BFO_0000050) at class level expresses that organs are parts of natural machines. The infinity claim is modeled as a quality rather than an OWL cardinality restriction to avoid reasoning intractability. The existing NaturalMaterialEntity class is reused as the parent for both NaturalMachine and Organ. Open questions remain about recursive composition (organs being machines themselves) and the relation to the existing Body individual.

proposal.utterance: Organized beings are evolved according to a preconceived plan.

entities.label: OrganizedBeing
entities.rationale: An organized being (e.g. a living organism) is a material entity with mass and spatial extent; it persists through time.

entities.label: PreconceivePlan
entities.rationale: A preconceived plan is an information artifact — a pattern of intentional design — that can in principle be instantiated in multiple bearers and is paradigmatically a generically dependent continuant.

entities.label: Evolution
entities.rationale: The development/unfolding of organized beings according to a plan is a process — it unfolds in time and has participants.

entities.label: PreconceivePlanConstraint
entities.rationale: The fact that evolution is guided by a preconceived plan introduces an internally-grounded directedness or constraint on the evolution process; this is best typed as a disposition inhering in the organized being or the process, and realized in the evolution process.

relations.rationale: The evolution process has organized beings as participants.
The preconceived-plan constraint disposition is realized in the evolution process.
A preconceived plan is a kind of Idea (already in the ontology as a generically dependent continuant), specifically a design idea.

open_questions: Is 'evolution' here intended in the Leibnizian/pre-Darwinian sense of preformation/unfolding (development of an individual organism according to a plan), or in the modern Darwinian sense of species change over time? This affects whether Evolution should be a sub-process of an organism's development or a population-level process.
Who or what holds the preconceived plan — is it God (already individual in the ontology) or some immanent design principle within organized beings?
Should PreconceivePlanConstraint inhere in OrganizedBeing, or in God, or in both? This is needed to assert the correct RO_0000052 (inheres in) triple.
Is 'organized being' equivalent to or a subclass of an existing class (e.g. NaturalMaterialEntity) in the ontology?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts three core ontological commitments: (1) there exist organized beings (material entities, BFO_0000040); (2) there is a preconceived plan (an information/design artifact, BFO_0000031, subsumed under the existing Idea class); and (3) organized beings evolve — i.e., undergo a directed development process (BFO_0000015) — in accordance with that plan. The directedness introduced by 'preconceived' is best captured as a disposition (BFO_0000016) that is realized in the evolution process. The plan itself is a generically dependent continuant (an information pattern) distinct from the disposition, though the two are closely related. Key open questions concern the intended sense of 'evolution' and the bearer of the preconceived plan.

proposal.utterance: Nature is the principle of motion and of rest.

entities.label: Nature
entities.rationale: In Aristotelian metaphysics (the source of this claim), Nature is an intrinsic, internally grounded principle of motion and rest in things that possess it — paradigmatically a disposition or capacity inhering in natural material entities. BFO Disposition (internally grounded realizable entity) best captures this: it is a capacity that is realized in processes of motion or rest.

entities.label: NaturalMotion
entities.rationale: Motion is a process (an occurrent unfolding in time). Nature, as a disposition, is realized in processes of natural motion.

entities.label: NaturalRest
entities.rationale: Rest (stasis, cessation of motion) is also a process-like state that unfolds over time; in BFO it is best modeled as a process or process boundary. Typed here as Process to parallel NaturalMotion and to allow realization of Nature.

relations.rationale: Nature as disposition is realized in processes of natural motion — the canonical BFO relation between a realizable entity and the process that realizes it.
Nature as disposition is equally realized in processes of natural rest, capturing the full Aristotelian claim that Nature is principle of both motion and rest.

PrincipleOfDetermination (already in the ontology as a Disposition subclass) is a natural parent for Nature qua determining principle; however, since PrincipleOfDetermination is a class and Nature is proposed as an individual, this types Nature under it — which also aligns with the existing SubstanceProgress and PrincipleOfDetermination classes already modeled as dispositions.

open_questions: Should 'Nature' be modeled as a class (a kind of disposition shared by all natural material entities) rather than a single individual? Aristotle seems to mean it as a universal principle, but representing it as an individual token disposition risks under-generalizing.
Is 'NaturalRest' better typed as a process boundary or a zero-change process, rather than a full BFO Process? BFO distinguishes ongoing processes from their temporal boundaries.
Should 'Nature' inhere in 'NaturalMaterialEntity' (already in the ontology) via RO_0000052, making explicit that only natural material entities bear this disposition?

The existing 'PrincipleOfDetermination' class is a Disposition — should 'Nature' be a subclass of it, or is PrincipleOfDetermination already a sufficient type for Nature without a separate individual?
proposal.rationale_summary: The Aristotelian claim 'Nature is the principle of motion and of rest' (Physics II.1) introduces Nature as an internally grounded, intrinsic capacity of natural material entities to move and rest by their own resources — precisely the BFO profile of a Disposition (BFO_0000016). I therefore mint Nature as an individual Disposition, typed also under the existing PrincipleOfDetermination class. To capture what Nature is a principle *of*, I introduce two process classes — NaturalMotion and NaturalRest — and assert that Nature is realized in both via BFO_0000054. Key open questions concern whether Nature should be a class rather than an individual, whether NaturalRest requires a different BFO type (process boundary vs. process), and whether an explicit inheres-in relation to NaturalMaterialEntity should be asserted.

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts three distinct ontological commitments: (1) there was a divine command in the past (a completed or at least initiated process: DivinePastCommand, individual of type BFO Process, with God as participant); (2) that command produced an effect that persists and continues to be causally operative in the present (PerdurantEffect, modeled as a Disposition because it is an internally grounded capacity or tendency that endures in a bearer even after the initiating process concluded); and (3) the present operation of that effect is itself an ongoing process (PerdurantEffectContinuation, a BFO Process realized from the Disposition). The existing individual 'God' and 'World' are reused. The relation between the past command and the perdurant effect is causal but BFO does not natively express causation; the realization relation (BFO_0000054) connects the disposition to its present process. The link of PerdurantEffectContinuation to BodyContinuousAction is tentative and flagged for user review.

This is best typed as a Disposition (BFO_0000016), an internally grounded realizable entity. It is similar in character to the existing individual ActiveForce but is explicitly named and given a broader cosmological scope. It is a named individual in Leibniz's system.

entities.label: NaturalPhenomenonProduction

entities.label: NaturalPhenomenon
entities.rationale: Phenomena produced by Nature are occurrents — happenings or appearances in the world. They are best typed as processes (BFO_0000015), consistent with Leibniz's phenomenalist framing where perceived phenomena are temporal occurrents rather than independent substances.

relations.rationale: Nature as a force/efficacy impressed on things is a disposition — an internally grounded realizable entity.
Nature as a disposition is realized in the process of natural phenomenon production — the 'producing phenomena' described in the utterance.
Instances of NaturalPhenomenon are parts of (or outputs within) NaturalPhenomenonProduction processes; phenomena are produced within these processes.

Is 'Nature' here sufficiently distinct from the existing individual 'ActiveForce' to warrant a separate individual, or should it be typed as the same individual or a subtype?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that Nature is a force or efficacy that God impresses upon created things, and that this force exists and produces phenomena. proposal.utterance: Bodies contain something besides uniform mass and its transportation.

entities.label: UniformMass
entities.rationale: Uniform mass (materia prima understood as homogeneous bulk extension) is a quality or property of material bodies in the Leibnizian context. Modeled as a Quality subclass since it characterizes the body as a bearer.

entities.label: Transportation
entities.rationale: Transportation (translatio / motion from place to place) is a process in which a body participates. Leibniz explicitly contrasts mere translatory motion with the deeper active principle in bodies.

entities.label: ActiveForceInBody
entities.rationale: The 'something besides' uniform mass and transportation that bodies contain is, for Leibniz, an active principle / force (vis activa). This is an internally grounded disposition inhering in the body, distinct from passive bulk and from mere locomotion. ActiveForce already exists as an individual; this is the corresponding class for the active-force-in-body concept.

entities.label: PassiveForceInBody
entities.rationale: Leibniz also posits a passive force (materia secunda / antitypia / resistance) in body that goes beyond mere uniform mass. Modeled as a Disposition because it is an internally grounded capacity to resist penetration and conserve bulk.

relations.rationale: The body (individual) bears the active force that is over and above uniform mass and transportation.
The body (individual) also bears a passive force / resistance, another element beyond mere uniform mass.
The body bears the quality of uniform mass (the Cartesian component Leibniz is contrasting against).
The body participates in transportation (translatory motion), the other element being contrasted.

PassiveForceInBody is a subclass of Disposition (BFO_0000016).

Should PassiveForceInBody be further subdivided into primary matter (antitypia / impenetrability) and secondary matter (inertia / resistance to acceleration), following Leibniz's own distinction?
Should UniformMass be subclassed under an existing class such as working:RealUnity or kept directly under BFO Quality?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance captures Leibniz's critique of the Cartesian reduction of body to extension (uniform mass) and motion (transportation): bodies must contain something more, namely active and passive forces (vis activa and vis passiva / materia secunda). I mint four new items: UniformMass (Quality, the Cartesian component being critiqued), Transportation (Process, local motion), ActiveForceInBody (Disposition, the immanent principle of activity beyond Cartesian mechanics), and PassiveForceInBody (Disposition, resistance/antitypia). entities.rationale: Vacuum in classical atomism is the void space through which atoms move — an empty spatial site. BFO Site (BFO_0000029) is the most fitting type for an empty place or region conceived as a container for material entities.

entities.label: RejectionOfAtoms
entities.rationale: The philosophical stance that atoms must be rejected is a doctrinal disposition — a normative commitment inhering in a theoretical position or thinker. Modeled as an individual disposition.

entities.label: RejectionOfVacuum
entities.rationale: The parallel philosophical stance that vacuum must be rejected, modeled as an individual disposition.

entities.label: DoctrinelRejection
entities.rationale: A class for doctrinal or philosophical rejections — normative commitments to deny the existence or acceptability of some entity kind. RejectionOfAtoms and RejectionOfVacuum are instances of this class.

This introduces at least four ontological commitments: (1) Happiness itself as a durable, internally-grounded condition — best typed as a BFO Disposition (BFO_0000016) since it is stable, borne by a subject, and enables further processes; (2) a PleasureCapacity — also a Disposition, realized in the process of experiencing Pleasure; (3) Pleasure — a mental process (MentalChange subclass) that is the realization of PleasureCapacity; (4) NecessaryGoods — the things whose possession grounds the condition; and (5) Possession as a Role, the relational status of the bearer with respect to NecessaryGoods. proposal.utterance: The senses can make known what is, but cannot make known what ought to be or what could not be otherwise.

entities.label: SensoryEpistemicCapacity
entities.rationale: The capacity of the senses to make known what is (contingent factual content) is an internally grounded disposition inhering in sensing beings. Modeled as a class of Disposition.

entities.label: NormativeContent
entities.rationale: What ought to be is a normative information content — a generically dependent continuant that can be instantiated in many bearers and does not depend on sensory experience for its epistemic ground. Modeled as a subclass of GDC (like Idea already in the ontology).

entities.label: NecessaryTruth
entities.rationale: What could not be otherwise — necessary truths — are informational contents whose modal status is not contingent. They are generically dependent continuants (like Idea) not grounded in sensory givenness.

entities.label: ContingentFact
entities.rationale: What is — contingent states of affairs known through sensation — is a generically dependent continuant (informational content) whose epistemic access is grounded in the senses.

entities.label: SensoryEpistemicLimitation
entities.rationale: The incapacity of the senses to ground normative or necessary content is itself a stable dispositional property of sensing beings — an intrinsic limitation inhering in them.

relations.rationale: SensoryEpistemicCapacity is a more specific kind of ExternalSense already in the ontology, capturing the positive epistemic function of the senses.
SensoryEpistemicLimitation is also a dispositional property of the same faculties as ExternalSense, representing their bounded scope.
ContingentFact is a kind of Idea (GDC) whose content is empirically accessible — the object of sensory epistemic capacity.
NormativeContent is a kind of Idea (GDC) — it is an information pattern not derivable from the senses alone.
NecessaryTruth is a kind of Idea (GDC) representing what could not be otherwise — modal necessities inaccessible to sensation.

open_questions: Is this utterance from Leibniz specifically (e.g., New Essays on Human Understanding, alluding to the Kantian-style distinction between empirical and a priori knowledge)? If so, should we mint an individual for 'Leibniz' or a specific text to anchor these assertions?

Should NormativeContent and NecessaryTruth be kept as separate classes, or unified under a single 'NonEmpiricalContent' class? Leibniz distinguishes necessary truths (logic/math) from normative truths (ethics), but they share the feature of being beyond sensory grounding.
Is 'SensoryEpistemicCapacity' meant to be an individual (the one capacity) or a class (a kind of disposition)? Given the general philosophical claim, class seems right, but please confirm.
Should we model the relation between SensoryEpistemicCapacity and ContingentFact using a custom 'grounds knowledge of' relation, or is that beyond the current scope?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts an epistemological distinction: the senses can reveal contingent facts (what is), but cannot reveal normative content (what ought to be) or necessary truths (what could not be otherwise). In BFO terms, the epistemic capacity of the senses is a Disposition (BFO_0000016) inhering in sensing beings — modeled as SensoryEpistemicCapacity, a subclass of the already-existing ExternalSense. Its limitation is similarly a dispositional property, SensoryEpistemicLimitation. The three kinds of content — ContingentFact, NormativeContent, and NecessaryTruth — are modeled as subclasses of Idea (which is already typed as BFO_0000031, generically dependent continuant), reflecting the Leibnizian and broadly rationalist view that necessary and normative truths are informational contents whose authority is not empirically grounded. No individuals are asserted; all commitments are at the class level, reflecting the general philosophical claim rather than a particular case.

proposal.utterance: Reason aids us in extending knowledge beyond immediate experience.

entities.label: Knowledge Extension
entities.rationale: Extending knowledge beyond immediate experience is a process — an occurrent that unfolds in time, involving the active deployment of Reason to generate new epistemic states.

entities.label: ImmediateExperience
entities.rationale: Immediate experience (sensory/perceptual acquaintance) is itself a process or collection of processes. It is the baseline from which Reason extends knowledge. This is distinct from the perceptual sub-classes already present (ColorPerception, etc.) as it denotes the aggregate experiential process.

relations.rationale: The KnowledgeExtension process has Reason as a participant: Reason is realized/deployed during the process of extending knowledge. Reason already exists as an individual of type BFO_0000016 (Disposition); it participates in KnowledgeExtension.
Reason (a disposition/realizable) is realized in the KnowledgeExtension process, capturing Leibniz's claim that Reason's function is precisely this extension beyond immediate experience.
Extending knowledge is a species of Thinking (already a MentalChange subclass), since it is a higher-order cognitive process going beyond perception.
Immediate experience is a subclass of Perceiving (already present), representing the direct sensory/experiential baseline that Reason transcends.

open_questions: Should 'Knowledge Extension' be modeled as a class of processes (generalizing across all acts of reasoning beyond experience) or as a specific individual process associated with Leibniz's account? Currently proposed as a class.

Should 'ImmediateExperience' remain a subclass of Perceiving, or should it also encompass memory and other non-inferential mental states? This depends on how broadly Leibniz intends 'immediate experience' here.

Reason is currently typed as an individual of BFO_0000016 (Disposition). Should it also be typed as a class (i.e., a kind of disposition that any rational soul can bear), or remain a singular individual representing the universal faculty? The current model treats it as a singular faculty-individual.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts a functional claim: Reason (already an individual disposition in the ontology) is the faculty by which knowledge is extended beyond what immediate experience (perception) delivers. This introduces two new classes: KnowledgeExtension as a subclass of Thinking (the process of going beyond perceptual data via inference/reason), and ImmediateExperience as a subclass of Perceiving (the perceptual baseline). The key ontological commitment is that Reason, as a realizable/disposition, is realized in KnowledgeExtension processes. The participation relation (RO_0000057) and realizability relation (BFO_0000054) together capture Leibniz's claim that rational inference extends beyond sensory limits. No new individuals are minted; Reason is reused from the known individuals list.

entities.label: Induction
entities.rationale: Induction is an epistemic process — a type of reasoning process that unfolds in time as a cognitive activity. Modeled as a subclass of BFO Process (and thus of MentalChange is plausible, but Induction can also occur in formal argument, so a direct Process subclass is safer).

entities.rationale: An example is an information artifact — a pattern of content that can be instantiated in multiple bearers. It is best modeled as a Generically Dependent Continuant (like Idea or LegalDocument already in the ontology).

entities.rationale: A proof is an information artifact — a structured argument whose content can be copied or instantiated. Modeled as a Generically Dependent Continuant.

entities.label: PerfectProof
entities.rationale: A perfect proof is a species of Proof distinguished by the quality of being conclusive/necessary. Modeled as a subclass of Proof.

entities.label: Geometry
entities.rationale: Geometry as a formal discipline is a body of information content — a system of propositions and methods. Modeled as a Generically Dependent Continuant (a formal/scientific discipline as an information artifact).

entities.label: Arithmetic
entities.rationale: Arithmetic as a formal discipline is analogously a body of information content. Modeled as a Generically Dependent Continuant.

entities.label: InductiveEvidenceSufficiency
entities.rationale: The claim asserts that induction and examples lack the disposition to produce perfect proofs in formal sciences. This epistemic insufficiency is a disposition (or lack thereof) inhering in the inductive process. Modeling the concept of 'capacity to yield perfect proof' as a Disposition class allows the assertion that Induction lacks (does not instantiate) InductiveEvidenceSufficiency for geometry/arithmetic.

relations.rationale: PerfectProof is a specialization of Proof.
Induction is a process — a cognitive/argumentative process unfolding in time.
Example is a generically dependent continuant — an information artifact.
Geometry as a formal body of knowledge is a generically dependent continuant.
Arithmetic as a formal body of knowledge is a generically dependent continuant.

open_questions: Should Induction be modeled as a subclass of the existing MentalChange (cognitive process) or kept as a direct subclass of BFO Process to allow for formal/non-mental inductive argument as well?
Should Geometry and Arithmetic be modeled as individuals (specific disciplines) rather than classes, since they refer to unique formal systems?

The claim is essentially a negative universal — 'induction/examples are never sufficient for perfect proof in formal sciences.' Should this be expressed as an OWL axiom (e.g., disjointness or a universal restriction) or left as an open annotation/comment?
Is 'perfect proof' here specifically Leibniz's notion of demonstration from necessary truths, implying a connection to the existing NecessaryExistenceQuality or PrincipleOfDetermination individuals?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts an epistemic principle: inductive reasoning and examples alone are insufficient to produce perfect (i.e., demonstrative, necessary) proofs in geometry and arithmetic. The core claim — that induction/examples do not have the disposition to yield perfect proofs in these domains — is a negative assertion best captured via OWL restrictions or annotations once the user confirms these typings. As a standing, internally-grounded capacity it fits BFO Disposition (BFO_0000016). Note existing working:Perceiving (MentalChange/Process) captures the occurrent act; this class captures the dispositional/capacity reading referenced in the utterance. The existing perception-related classes (ColorPerception, FigurePerception, MotionPerception, OdorPerception, Perceiving) are all subtypes of MentalChange (Process); a dispositional Perception class is distinct and new.

entities.label: PrincipleOfAction
entities.rationale: The 'principle of action or change' is the internal ground of a monad's transitions — an internally-grounded disposition to generate change. This is distinct from the existing working:PrincipleOfDetermination (which grounds determinate states) and working:ActiveForce (an individual). A class PrincipleOfAction covers the type. It is a subclass of BFO Disposition.

relations.rationale: ImmaterialSubstance is a kind of persisting entity; BFO_0000040 (Material entity) is the closest BFO class for a substance individual, pending resolution of the BFO typing tension noted in open_questions.

Leibniz's simple substances (monads) are the paradigm case of immaterial substances; SimpleSubstance is already in the ontology and should be placed under ImmaterialSubstance.

(An alternative is bearer-of, but since Perception is a class and ImmaterialSubstance is a class, a subClassOf + someValuesFrom restriction would be more precise — flagged in open_questions.)
The utterance asserts the principle of action/change is included in immaterial substances.

open_questions: BFO typing tension: BFO_0000040 (Material entity) is defined as having mass and spatial extent, which conflicts with 'immaterial'. The 'has part' relation (BFO_0000051) is used here class-to-class as shorthand. proposal.utterance: The existence of matter depends on an ultimate reason outside itself.

entities.label: Matter
entities.rationale: Matter as discussed by Leibniz is a specific material entity (the aggregate of extended, physical substance). Modeled as an individual of type NaturalMaterialEntity (itself a subclass of BFO material entity).

entities.label: ExternalReason
entities.rationale: An 'ultimate reason outside matter' is a ground or explanatory disposition that is not internal to material substance. It is modeled as a Disposition subclass (externally grounded capacity/ground), distinct from the Reason individual already in the ontology which is an instance. A new class is needed to type the relation properly.

entities.label: UltimateExternalReason
entities.rationale: The specific ultimate reason outside matter for its existence — a singular individual disposition (grounded in God per Leibniz). This individual encapsulates the ontological dependency claim.

entities.label: ExistenceOfMatter
entities.rationale: The existence of matter as an ongoing state/process — the being or persisting of matter — is modeled as a Process (occurrent) that can be said to be realized by or dependent on the UltimateExternalReason. BFO does not have a 'dependent existence' relation natively; modeling existence as a process allows us to express the dependency via BFO relations.

relations.rationale: Matter participates in the process of its own existence.

The process of matter's existence realizes the UltimateExternalReason — i.e., the ultimate external reason is the disposition/ground that is realized through matter's existing. This captures the dependence of matter's existence on an external ground.
The ultimate reason outside matter inheres in God, who is the necessary being bearing this ground. Leibniz explicitly identifies the sufficient reason for the world's existence with God.
ExternalReason is a subclass of BFO Disposition.

open_questions: Should 'Matter' here be typed as a class (general kind of material entity) rather than an individual, to cover all matter universally rather than a single instance?

Should 'ExistenceOfMatter' be modeled as a Quality or a process? BFO does allow 'existence' to be a quality inhering in an entity (e.g., a 'NecessaryExistenceQuality' is already in the ontology); should we instead say Matter bears a ContingentExistenceQuality that depends on (is grounded by) UltimateExternalReason?

Is the 'ultimate reason outside matter' to be identified directly with God (already in the ontology), or is it a distinct disposition that inheres in God? The current proposal models it as inhering in God.
Should we introduce a new BFO-compatible 'dependsOnForExistence' relation, or is the BFO 'realizes/is realized in' pattern sufficient here?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that matter's existence has an external ground — a sufficient reason that lies outside matter itself. In Leibniz's framework this is the core cosmological argument: contingent material existence requires an ultimate reason, which is God. I model Matter as an individual NaturalMaterialEntity, introduce a class ExternalReason (subclass of BFO Disposition) for grounds that are extrinsic to their subject, and mint an individual UltimateExternalReason of that class. The process ExistenceOfMatter is introduced so we can use BFO's 'realizes/is realized in' relational pattern to express that matter's existing realizes (is grounded by) the UltimateExternalReason, which in turn inheres in God (already in the ontology). Key open questions concern whether Matter should be a class vs. individual, and whether a quality-based rather than process-based model of 'existence' would be more consistent with the already-present NecessaryExistenceQuality individual.

proposal.utterance: Immaterial finite substances are united to organs and accompany matter.

entities.label: ImmaterialFiniteSubstance
entities.rationale: Immaterial finite substances are a subkind of ImmaterialSubstance (already in the ontology), distinguished by being finite. They are still typed as material entity (BFO_0000040) via inheritance from ImmaterialSubstance. As individual substances they are independent continuants.

entities.label: Organ
entities.rationale: An organ is a material entity (biological body part) that the immaterial finite substance is united to. Needs to be introduced as a class to support the union relation.

entities.label: UnionWithOrgan
entities.rationale: The 'being united to an organ' is an internally grounded relational property of the immaterial finite substance — a disposition inhering in it that is realized in conjunction with a material organ. Modeled as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) subclass.

entities.label: AccompanimentOfMatter
entities.rationale: The property of 'accompanying matter' is an internally grounded disposition inhering in the immaterial finite substance, expressing its constant co-presence with material substance. Leibniz's claim is that immaterial substances are never without an accompanying body/matter.

relations.rationale: ImmaterialFiniteSubstance is a subclass of ImmaterialSubstance, adding the constraint of finitude.
UnionWithOrgan is a disposition class, subclass of BFO Disposition.
AccompanimentOfMatter is a disposition class, subclass of BFO Disposition.

The UnionWithOrgan disposition inheres in (is a property of) ImmaterialFiniteSubstance — expressed as a domain restriction: instances of UnionWithOrgan inhere in instances of ImmaterialFiniteSubstance.
The AccompanimentOfMatter disposition inheres in ImmaterialFiniteSubstance.
ImmaterialFiniteSubstance bears UnionWithOrgan and AccompanimentOfMatter dispositions — expressed via bearer-of restrictions on those disposition classes.

open_questions: Should 'ImmaterialFiniteSubstance' be further restricted to be disjoint from NaturalMaterialEntity, or does the existing ImmaterialSubstance parent already handle that?
Is 'Organ' here specifically a biological organ (body part of a living organism), or does it have a broader Leibnizian sense of any instrument through which the soul acts?

Should 'UnionWithOrgan' be modeled as a Role (externally grounded) rather than a Disposition, given that the union seems to depend on the relation to an external organ rather than intrinsic structure?

Does 'accompanying matter' mean that the immaterial finite substance is spatially co-located with (or within) a material body, i.e., should we assert a BFO site/location relation between ImmaterialFiniteSubstance and some material region?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts three ontological commitments about immaterial finite substances: (1) they are a distinct subkind of immaterial substance, (2) they are united to organs (material body parts), and (3) they always accompany matter. I introduce ImmaterialFiniteSubstance as a new class (subclass of the existing ImmaterialSubstance) to capture the finitude qualifier. The organ-union and matter-accompaniment are each modeled as Disposition subclasses inhering in ImmaterialFiniteSubstance, because in Leibnizian metaphysics these are stable, internally-grounded features of such substances rather than externally imposed roles. The class Organ is introduced as a material entity class to serve as the target of the union relation. The last proposed relation in the relations list (bearer-of) is a placeholder for OWL restrictions expressing that every ImmaterialFiniteSubstance bears both dispositions; the reasoner should be asked to validate the subClassOf chain and disjointness with purely material classes.

proposal.utterance: Souls or active forms are found everywhere in matter.

entities.label: ActiveForm
entities.rationale: An 'active form' in the Leibnizian sense is an internally-grounded capacity/principle that makes a material entity what it is; Disposition (BFO_0000016) best captures this intrinsic, realizable character. It generalises both souls (already individual) and sub-sentient active forms in matter.

entities.label: Matter
entities.rationale: Matter as a kind of material entity (NaturalMaterialEntity is the closest existing parent, but 'Matter' as a class distinct from organised natural bodies is needed to ground the 'found in matter' relation).

relations.rationale: ActiveForm is a subclass of Disposition, as justified above.
Matter is a kind of NaturalMaterialEntity already in the ontology.
The utterance equates souls with active forms; asserting that the individual Soul is of type ActiveForm captures this identification.
Restatement for clarity: every active form is a disposition.

open_questions: Should 'ActiveForm' be a subclass of the existing 'Potentiality' or 'PrincipleOfAction' classes already in the ontology, rather than directly under BFO Disposition? They seem closely related.

The claim 'souls/active forms are found everywhere in matter' implies a universal distribution axiom (every instance of Matter has at least one ActiveForm inhering in it). Shall we assert this as an OWL subclass axiom (Matter subClassOf bearerOf some ActiveForm)?
Is 'Matter' here the same as 'NaturalMaterialEntity', or does it specifically denote unorganised/primary matter (materia prima) as distinct from compound bodies?
Should individual Soul be re-typed as ActiveForm, or should its existing BFO_0000040 type be replaced or supplemented?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance makes two claims: (1) souls and active forms are the same kind of thing, and (2) instances of this kind are distributed throughout all matter. To capture (1) I introduce the class ActiveForm as a subclass of BFO Disposition (BFO_0000016), reflecting an intrinsic, internally-grounded capacity; I then assert that the existing individual Soul is of type ActiveForm. To capture (2) I introduce the class Matter as a subclass of NaturalMaterialEntity. A universal distribution axiom (every Matter bears some ActiveForm) is flagged as an open question rather than committed immediately, because it would require a subclass axiom with an existential restriction that the user should confirm. Existing classes Potentiality and PrincipleOfAction are candidates for parentage of ActiveForm and are raised as open questions.

proposal.utterance: Force and action are found everywhere in matter.

entities.label: Force
entities.rationale: Force as a general capacity or power found in matter is best typed as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) — an internally grounded realizable that inheres in its bearer (material entities). This aligns with Leibnizian 'force' as an immanent capacity of substances. Note: working:ActiveForce already exists as an individual; Force as a class generalizes over all forces in matter.

entities.label: Action
entities.rationale: Action is the actualization or exercise of force — a happening unfolding in time. In BFO terms, this is a Process (BFO_0000015). It is the realization of a Force/Disposition inhering in matter.

PerceptionDevelopment realizes the GoodEvilOrientation disposition: the process of developing perceptions realizes the soul's disposition toward goods and evils, i.e. the direction according to which development proceeds.
The GoodEvilOrientation disposition inheres in the Soul, which is the bearer of the law-governed directedness toward goods and evils.

proposal.utterance: Nothing ever occurs without a cause or determining reason.

entities.label: PrincipleOfSufficientReason
entities.rationale: The Principle of Sufficient Reason is an internally-grounded, general constraint on the occurrence of any process or state — every occurrence is grounded in a determining reason or cause. This is best captured as a Disposition (internally grounded tendency/constraint) at the class level, representing the general principle that each occurrence has such a ground.

entities.label: DeterminingReason
entities.rationale: A determining reason is the specific ground or cause that explains why a particular occurrence takes place rather than not. It inheres in the bearer (substance or entity) that produces or grounds the effect. Modeled as a Disposition subclass since it is an internally-grounded capacity/ground for producing an effect.

entities.label: Occurrence
entities.rationale: An occurrence is any happening or event that unfolds in time. BFO Process is the appropriate type. This class represents the general domain of things the PSR governs.

relations.rationale: A determining reason is a specific instantiation or subtype of the general Principle of Sufficient Reason — each occurrence has its own determining reason, which is an instance of this broader principle.

The Principle of Sufficient Reason is a more specific formulation of the already-existing PrincipleOfDetermination class, which captures the general notion of what determines a substance's states. PSR is a subclass of it.

An occurrence in the Leibnizian sense is a kind of SubstanceOperation — a happening produced by or within substance. Relating Occurrence as a subclass of the existing SubstanceOperation captures this.

open_questions: Should PrincipleOfSufficientReason be treated as a single named individual (the universal metaphysical principle, like existing 'God' or 'TheOne') rather than a class, given that Leibniz treats it as a single universal law?

Should DeterminingReason be modeled as a Disposition (internally grounded in the bearer-substance) or as a Role (externally ascribed to an event or cause)? The Leibnizian usage suggests it is intrinsic to the substance/bearer, favoring Disposition.

Is 'Occurrence' meant to cover all processes (BFO_0000015) or only contingent events as opposed to necessary ones? This affects whether it should be a proper subclass of SubstanceOperation or a broader Process subclass.

Should there be an explicit relation (e.g., a custom object property 'hasDeterminingReason') between Occurrence and DeterminingReason to formally encode that every occurrence has at least one determining reason?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance expresses Leibniz's Principle of Sufficient Reason (PSR): every occurrence has a determining reason or cause. Three new classes are proposed: (1) PrincipleOfSufficientReason as a Disposition subclass (and subclass of the existing PrincipleOfDetermination), representing the universal metaphysical constraint; (2) DeterminingReason as a Disposition subclass of PrincipleOfSufficientReason, representing the specific ground inhering in a bearer that explains a particular occurrence; and (3) Occurrence as a Process subclass (related to the existing SubstanceOperation) representing any happening subject to the PSR. No new individuals are minted because the PSR is expressed here as a universal law (class-level), not a named singular entity, though the open questions flag whether it could alternatively be treated as a named individual analogous to 'God' or 'TheOne'. The PrincipleOfDetermination class already in the ontology is the natural parent for PSR.

proposal.utterance: Humans are always infallibly led to that which strikes them most, but not necessarily.

entities.label: InclinationToMostStriking
entities.rationale: The claim is that humans have a disposition to be led toward whatever strikes them most forcefully. This is an internally grounded tendency of the bearer (the human/soul), fitting BFO Disposition. It is always triggered (infallible) but Leibniz qualifies it as not metaphysically necessary, so it remains a disposition rather than a law-like necessity.

entities.label: MoralNecessity
entities.rationale: The qualification 'infallibly but not necessarily' marks a distinction between moral/practical necessity (certain but compatible with freedom) and absolute/metaphysical necessity. Leibniz's 'moral necessity' is a disposition-like constraint that reliably determines action without abolishing contingency. Modeled as a subclass of Disposition.

relations.rationale: InclinationToMostStriking is a specific kind of Potentiality (already in the ontology as a subclass of Disposition), since it is the human/soul's latent directedness toward its strongest percept, making it a species of Potentiality-as-disposition.

Moral necessity, like NaturalConstancy, represents a reliable but non-absolute determining principle; subclassing under NaturalConstancy (already a Disposition) captures this reliable-but-contingent character.
The infallible inclination toward what strikes most is precisely an instance of moral necessity: certain in outcome but not absolutely (metaphysically) necessary.

open_questions: Should 'what strikes them most' (the strongest percept/representation) be modeled as a distinct quality or is it captured within existing MentalAffection?
Is 'infallibly' intended to express a universal claim about all humans (all instances of Person) or about rational souls specifically? Should we add a restriction axiom on Person or Soul?
Should MoralNecessity be distinguished from AbsoluteNecessity (metaphysical necessity) as a sibling class, or is that distinction handled purely by annotation?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance expresses Leibniz's doctrine that humans are always determined by their strongest representation ('what strikes them most'), yet this determination is moral/practical rather than absolute (metaphysical) necessity—compatible with freedom. Ontologically this introduces two new Disposition subclasses: InclinationToMostStriking (the reliable directedness of the soul/human toward its strongest percept) and MoralNecessity (the modality of that determination—infallible yet contingent). InclinationToMostStriking is placed under the existing Potentiality class (itself a Disposition) to capture its character as a latent directedness, and it is also made a subclass of MoralNecessity to capture the infallibility-without-absolute-necessity qualifier. MoralNecessity is placed under NaturalConstancy to signal its reliable but non-absolute character. No new individuals are minted; Freedom and Reason already in the ontology provide context but no new relations to them are asserted without further textual warrant.

proposal.utterance: God is always infallibly led to the best by moral necessity, not absolute necessity.

entities.label: MoralNecessity
entities.rationale: Moral necessity in Leibniz is the internally-grounded disposition of God to always choose the best; it is not an external constraint but a feature of God's nature. BFO Disposition (internally grounded realizable) is the best fit. Modeled as an individual inhering in God.

entities.label: AbsoluteNecessity
entities.rationale: Absolute necessity is the contrasting concept — a logically constraining necessity from which there is no alternative. Modeled as a disposition individual to represent the kind of compulsion Leibniz says does NOT apply to God. Introduced to anchor the negation expressed in the utterance.

entities.label: ChoosingTheBest
entities.rationale: Being 'infallibly led to the best' describes a process of divine choice/action. Modeled as a subclass of SubstanceOperation (already in the ontology for substance-level activities).

relations.rationale: Moral necessity inheres in God as an internally-grounded disposition of God's will/nature.
God is the bearer of MoralNecessity (inverse of inheres-in).
MoralNecessity is realized in processes of ChoosingTheBest — it is what infallibly leads God to choose the best outcome.
ChoosingTheBest is a kind of SubstanceOperation (divine substance's self-directed activity).

open_questions: Should AbsoluteNecessity be retained as an individual (a kind of necessity that does NOT apply to God) or should it be introduced only to support a negation axiom (e.g., owl:complementOf or a disjointness axiom with MoralNecessity)? BFO does not natively support negation of property-holding, so the representation of 'not absolute necessity' may need an OWL disjointness axiom outside BFO proper.

Is 'infallibly led' meant to capture that God has no freedom to choose otherwise (a strong reading), or that God always in fact chooses the best while retaining freedom (Leibniz's actual view)? The latter would keep Freedom (already in the ontology) compatible with MoralNecessity, and we could add a relation asserting that Freedom and MoralNecessity both inhere in God without conflict.
Should ChoosingTheBest be modeled as a class of processes or as a single individual process (i.e., God's eternal/ongoing act of optimization)?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance makes three ontological claims: (1) God possesses moral necessity as an internally-grounded disposition that infallibly directs divine choice; (2) this disposition is realized in a class of processes of choosing the best; (3) absolute necessity — a stronger, logically compulsory kind of necessity — is explicitly excluded as a property of God. MoralNecessity and AbsoluteNecessity are both modeled as BFO Disposition individuals (internally grounded realizables), since they represent features of God's nature rather than externally imposed roles. ChoosingTheBest is introduced as a class of processes (subclass of the existing SubstanceOperation) in which MoralNecessity is realized. The existing individual God is reused. The negation of absolute necessity cannot be directly expressed in BFO relational triples alone; an open question flags the need for an OWL disjointness or complementOf axiom.

proposal.utterance: Perfect equilibrium between options is impossible because the universe is not partitionable into equal parts.

entities.label: PerfectEquilibrium
entities.rationale: Perfect equilibrium between options (as in Buridan's ass / indifference of the will) is a disposition or potential state that would ground equally balanced choice; typed as Disposition because it is an internally grounded capacity/tendency of a substance or system, here asserted to be impossible.

entities.label: UniversalPartition
entities.rationale: The act of partitioning the universe into equal parts is a process (a hypothetical decomposition process); the utterance asserts this process cannot produce equal parts, grounding the impossibility of perfect equilibrium.

entities.label: EqualPartitionQuality
entities.rationale: The property of being partitioned into equal parts is a quality (measurable, comparative property) that the universe is asserted to lack; needed to represent the impossibility claim.

relations.rationale: PerfectEquilibrium is a subclass of Disposition, the BFO type for internally grounded potentials.
UniversalPartition is a subclass of Process.
EqualPartitionQuality is a subclass of Quality.
Reusing existing individual World (the universe) as the bearer; no new assertion needed beyond linking.

open_questions: Is this utterance specifically encoding Leibniz's Principle of Sufficient Reason (PSR) argument against perfect indifference — i.e., that because no two parts of the universe are equal, there is always a sufficient reason to prefer one option? If so, should we mint a 'PrincipleOfSufficientReason' class or individual?

Should 'PerfectEquilibrium' be typed as a Quality (a property that could inhere in an agent's deliberative state) rather than a Disposition? The equilibrium is more of a relational property of the option-set than a grounded capacity.

Does 'impossible' here mean logically impossible or merely nomologically impossible? This affects whether we should add a negation axiom (owl:Nothing equivalence) or a contingent constraint disposition.
Is 'universe' here the individual working:World, or a more abstract totality? Should we assert working:World lacks working:EqualPartitionQuality via an explicit negative property axiom?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts two connected metaphysical claims: (1) perfect equilibrium between options is impossible, and (2) the ground of that impossibility is that the universe cannot be divided into perfectly equal parts. This maps onto Leibniz's Principle of Sufficient Reason and his rejection of Buridan's-ass-style indifference. I mint three new classes: PerfectEquilibrium (a Disposition, since it would be an internally grounded potential for indifferent choice), UniversalPartition (a Process, the hypothetical act of dividing the universe into equal parts), and EqualPartitionQuality (a Quality that the universe is asserted to lack). The existing individual World is the relevant bearer. The impossibility claim is noted in open_questions since OWL negation axioms require explicit modeling decisions. I conservatively represent the structural commitments without overcommitting to the logical modality of the impossibility.

proposal.utterance: There is always something which determines choice between contradictories, even if we cannot perceive all impressions.

entities.label: SufficientDetermination
entities.rationale: The claim that something always determines choice between contradictories expresses a disposition or internally-grounded capacity: a sufficient reason or determining principle that fixes which alternative is actualized. It is a subclass of the existing PrincipleOfDetermination disposition class.

entities.label: Choice
entities.rationale: Choice between contradictories is an occurrent mental process, a subclass of Willing (already in the ontology). It is the process that SufficientDetermination is realized in.

entities.label: Impression
entities.rationale: Impressions in Leibniz are the minute perceptual qualities borne by a monad/soul. They are specifically dependent qualities inhering in the bearer (soul), and are a subclass of MentalAffection.

relations.rationale: SufficientDetermination is a species of PrincipleOfDetermination: the claim is that every choice has some determining principle, even if imperceptible.
A choice is a specific kind of willing process in which one of two contradictory alternatives is selected.
Impressions are mental affections, specifically the minute perceptions that may not rise to conscious awareness.

proposal.utterance: Eternal truths are necessary and proceed from the infinite nature of God.

entities.label: EternalTruth
entities.rationale: Eternal truths are necessary propositional/informational contents that can be instantiated in many minds or texts; they are patterns that can be copied, making them generically dependent continuants. They are not processes or material entities.

entities.label: NecessityQuality
entities.rationale: Necessity is a property that inheres in eternal truths — it is a quality characterising them as logically/metaphysically necessary rather than contingent.

entities.label: InfiniteNature
entities.rationale: Leibniz's 'infinite nature of God' is the intrinsic ground or source from which eternal truths proceed — an internally-grounded capacity/disposition of God. Treated as an individual because it refers to a specific, unique attribute of the individual God.

relations.rationale: NecessityQuality is a subclass of Quality (BFO_0000019).
EternalTruth is a subclass of Generically Dependent Continuant.
God (existing individual, BFO_0000040) is the bearer of InfiniteNature, which inheres in God as a disposition.
InfiniteNature inheres in God (inverse of bearer-of).

open_questions: Should EternalTruth be a class (a kind of truth) or an individual? In Leibniz there are many eternal truths (e.g., mathematical truths), so a class seems right — but do you want a specific named individual for 'eternal truths in general' (like TheOne)?

The claim that eternal truths 'proceed from' the infinite nature of God suggests a causal/grounding relation not captured by standard BFO predicates. Should we introduce a custom 'groundedIn' or 'proceedsFrom' object property for this dependence, or approximate it with RO_0000052 (inheres in) or BFO_0000054 (realized in)?
NecessityQuality inheres in instances of EternalTruth — should we also assert this as an OWL axiom (EternalTruth subClassOf bearerOf some NecessityQuality)?

Is 'InfiniteNature' best typed as a Disposition (internally grounded capacity of God) or as a Quality (a measurable property of God)? It functions more like a source/ground, which leans toward Disposition, but please confirm.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts three ontological commitments: (1) there exist eternal truths, which are necessary propositional contents — best typed as a class of Generically Dependent Continuants (BFO_0000031) since they are information-like patterns grounded in minds and language; (2) these truths have necessity as an intrinsic property — modelled as a Quality class (NecessityQuality, BFO_0000019) that inheres in instances of EternalTruth; and (3) they proceed from the infinite nature of God — modelled as an individual Disposition (InfiniteNature, BFO_0000016) that inheres in the already-existing individual God. The 'proceeds from' relation is the most ontologically challenging part: BFO has no direct 'grounds' or 'proceeds from' predicate, so I have used bearer-of/inheres-in to anchor InfiniteNature to God, but a custom object property may ultimately be needed to express the generative dependence of EternalTruth instances on God's nature.
